# Strategy Lead

**The role**

We’re looking for a Strategy Lead, within our EMEA Journey Strategy team, who asks sharp questions, gets to the heart of a business challenge and gives people a clear direction to act on.

You’ll put buyer journey and experience mapping at the heart of strategic work for leading B2B technology brands. You will lead insights, value prop and messaging development, content planning and experience mapping, connecting audience insight with compelling ideas and practical plans across the customer journey. Collaboration is central to the role: you’ll work closely with clients and our CX, creative, content, media, communications and technology specialists to shape the work together. You’ll stay involved through delivery, making sure the thinking holds up in practice.

**What you will do**

* Uncover the insight that shapes the strategy. Interrogate the brief and our clients’ businesses, drawing on audience research, SME interviews, competitor analysis, market and cultural insight, platform data and JourneyLab. Connect the evidence, challenge assumptions and identify the opportunities that should guide strategic direction.

* Lead buyer journey and experience mapping. Use research, JourneyLab and client collaboration to map how buying groups make decisions: who is involved, what they need, feel and encounter, and where progress stalls. Translate those insights into experience maps that define how the brand should respond across touchpoints, guiding creative, content, channels and activation.

* Develop value propositions and messaging. Define why a brand, product or solution matters to its audience and what makes it different. Turn that into clear value propositions and messaging frameworks, with relevant benefits and credible proof points for different buying group roles.

* Be a strategic partner to the creative team. Write and deliver inspiring creative briefs, bring audience insight into idea development and work alongside creatives to explore, challenge and sharpen concepts. Stay involved from the first conversation through to execution, helping distinctive ideas express the proposition and connect across the customer journey.

* Plan experiences with a clear purpose. Audit existing content assets and experiences, identify gaps and develop content themes, editorial plans and recommendations for formats, channels and sequencing around audience needs and journey stages.

* Connect channels around the buyer. Develop integrated communications and audience growth plans across paid, owned and earned channels, working with specialists to define where the brand should show up, the role of each channel and how activity builds reach, engagement and preference across the journey.

* Bring people and perspectives together. Build shared ownership with clients and specialists across Pretzl. Lead workshops, interview SMEs, present a persuasive strategic story and work through competing views constructively.

* Make the strategy count. Agree measures of success, connect activity to business outcomes and use learning to improve the work. Articulate the value of our thinking and identify opportunities to deepen client partnerships.

* Strengthen our practice. Share useful thinking and help evolve our methods, using data and AI responsibly while keeping human needs central.

**Who will thrive here**

You could be a Strategist ready to step up, a Strategy Lead looking to broaden your experience, or a writer or account lead already doing some of your best work in strategy. We’re open to different career paths. What matters is the experience, judgement and collaborative approach you bring.

Irrespective of your background you are curious about people and care about the craft of strategy. You make sense of complexity and turn it into thinking that inspires people and helps them act. You’re comfortable leading the work, getting stuck into the detail and building on the expertise of others.

* Experience in B2B marketing. You’ve worked with complex businesses, ideally technology brands, in an agency or comparable client-facing environment. You understand how buying groups make decisions and how marketing helps.

* Breadth of strategic thinking. Your experience spans several areas of strategy, such as audience insight, brand positioning, buyer journeys, content and integrated communications planning across paid, owned and earned channels. You can connect these disciplines and judge which approach a challenge needs.

* A talent for making complexity compelling. You get to grips with technical offerings and explain their value through simple, distinctive audience benefits. You can demonstrate how your thinking has shaped value propositions and messaging.

* A collaborative approach. You build strong relationships with creative teams and specialists across disciplines. You listen, welcome different perspectives and help others build on your thinking to make the work better.

* The ability to lead and influence. You bring clarity to ambiguous challenges, give teams direction and build client confidence. You can explain and defend your recommendations while remaining open to challenge.

* Research skills and sound judgement. You’re confident working with qualitative and quantitative evidence from audience, market and competitor research. You can assess sources, spot patterns and turn findings into a clear strategic point of view, balancing audience needs with commercial realities. You’re curious about how data, technology and AI can strengthen the work.

**Why join Pretzl**

You’ll help leading B2B technology brands tackle complex marketing challenges, alongside specialists with deep sector experience. There’s room to build your craft, shape our journey strategy practice and see your thinking come to life through close collaboration with the people around you.

**Introduction to NFU Mutual**  
NFU Mutual offers a wide range of products and services, including general insurance, life, pensions and investments and has been providing quality insurance for its customers, for over 110 years.  We carefully balance delivering excellent service to our customers whilst ensuring the business is run effectively.  As a mutual, supporting our customers and paying their claims comes first.  We are a top ten UK insurance company and the UK’s largest rural insurer, with an agency network of over 250 local offices.

  

**About the Agency**  
As a local agency of NFU Mutual we deliver a first-class service, and sell their product range across our region, to customers old and new, who are at the core of everything we do. We are a business where honesty, integrity, and trust are at the heart of our values. We champion the personal approach to customer service that NFU Mutual are famous for.

  

An exciting opportunity has now arisen within the Central-South Warwickshire & Pershore Agency.

  

**Our five Non-Negotiables are how we work, and how we choose people:**

  

Passion, Strive for Better, Ownership, Honesty and Celebrate Success.

  

Every role here is built on them, and this one is no exception.

## About the role

You will keep and grow our key farming General insurance (GI) accounts and, lead our NFU team to manage and grow our NFU memberships, and take a senior role across our NFU branches. It is a senior role with real influence over how we serve farming members. This is how our Non-Negotiables show up in the day to day.

  

**Passion**

**Ownership**

•    Own the retention of your key accounts and the quality of your team’s service.  
•    Work with account handlers, the accounts administrator and the claims manager to keep accounts running smoothly.  
•    Take senior responsibility alongside the Group Secretaries for our 5 NFU branches across Warwickshire and Worcestershire, with a focus on Evesham, giving a minimum of 10 hours a week to supporting NFU members. This includes branch and county meetings and events, generally in the evenings and at weekends.

  

**Honesty**  
•    Give the best advice whatever the commercial outcome, and sell professionally and compliantly to the standards of NFU Mutual, the T&C scheme and our regulators.  
•    Follow the NFU Mutual General Insurance Compliance Manual, the Agent’s Claims Guide and the Agency Guide, and handle customer money and credit control to NFU Mutual’s requirements.  
•    Give your team straight, fair feedback and be open about your own mistakes.  
Celebrate Success  
•    Recognise individual and team wins promptly and by name.  
•    Support the training and development of the NFU and Farming Exec team and celebrate their progress.  
•    Thank the branch officers, volunteers and NFU colleagues who help us serve members, and build strong relationships with County Advisers, Regional Directors and branch committees.

•    Strong existing and current relationships with NFU stakeholders.  
•    CII Certificate in Insurance (or equivalent), or the commitment to achieve it quickly.  
•    A strong compliance mindset, and confidence handling customer money and credit control.  
•    Confident use of Word, Excel and PowerPoint   
•    A full driving licence, willingness to travel, and willingness to attend NFU events in the evenings and at weekends.

  

**Desirable**  
•    Experience of the NFU Mutual agency network, the T&C scheme or NFU branch activity.  
•    A track record of growing a book of business through cross-sell.  
•    Existing relationships in the Warwickshire and Worcestershire farming community.

  

**What we are looking for in you**  
•    Passion: real interest in farming and rural communities, and pride in getting the detail right.  
•    Strive for Better: you see a quicker or better way and act without being asked, adapt when things change, and use feedback to improve.  
•    Ownership: you take responsibility for results, including your team’s, and solve problems rather than passing them on.  
•    Honesty: you do the right thing even when no one would notice if you didn’t, are straight with customers and colleagues, catch your own mistakes early and treat feedback as something to use rather than survive.  
•    Celebrate Success: you credit others, share the credit and notice good work without being prompted.

  

**Our commitment to you**  
You will have training and support to succeed in the role, support towards professional qualifications such as CII, regular 1:1s and reviews, and a team that recognises and celebrates success.

**Your impact begins here**

Lead a front-line scientific team that exploits human genetics, multi-omics, and patient data to deepen disease understanding and identify new opportunities for target discovery. As Associate Director, Disease and Target Biology, you will leverage your scientific and people leadership expertise to drive target discovery campaigns with our Therapy Areas and translate complex evidence into clear decisions. You and your team will work with the TAs to define the biological evidence needed to move targets and programmes forward across Type 2 Diabetes, Obesity, Cardiovascular, and Renal disease.

**What you'll bring**

You are an experienced scientific leader who can move confidently between detailed analysis, team development, and strategic decision-making. You bring strong expertise in human genetics and computational biology, along with the ability to explain complex evidence clearly to scientific and senior stakeholders.

Essential qualifications and experience:

* A PhD in human genetics, computational biology, genetic epidemiology, or a related discipline, together with substantial post-PhD experience.
* Experience combining genetics and omics with cohort or patient data to identify and stratify patient subgroups; and demonstrated experience applying this to actionable disease understanding and target discovery / validation.
* At least 5 years of leadership experience in drug/target discovery, with pharmaceutical, biomedical, or techbio industry experience strongly preferred.
* Experience leading and developing scientific teams, ideally across multiple locations, and comfortable remaining hands-on technically.
* Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to influence therapeutic area partners and senior leaders.

Useful, but not essential:

* Experience managing teams across sites or time zones.
* Direct experience in metabolic, cardiovascular, or renal disease.
* Familiarity with artificial intelligence and machine-learning approaches applied to biological and clinical data.
* An understanding of the drug discovery and development value chain.
* A strong publication record and standing in the external scientific community would also be valuable.

**What you'll do**

* Lead and develop a team of approximately seven scientists based across the UK and Denmark, taking responsibility for recruitment, performance, development, well-being and an effective cross-site working environment.
* Use human genetics, multi-omics and cohort or patient data to identify and stratify patient subgroups; applying results in pursuit of better disease understanding and testable hypotheses for target discovery.
* Co-lead scientific campaigns with therapeutic area teams, defining the biological evidence required to support or challenge hypotheses and enable programme decisions.
* Set the team's scientific and operational direction in partnership with Data Science leaders and colleagues across AI & Digital Innovation and Global Research.
* Guide the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning in disease biology, work with engineering teams on deployment, and provide scientific leadership for academic and biotechnology collaborations.

**Who you'll work with**

You will join the Disease and Target Biology team within ADI Data Science and report to Robert Kitchen. The role leads approximately seven direct reports with varying levels of seniority and specialist expertise across the UK and Denmark.

Your closest partners will include Therapy Area colleagues working in Type 2 Diabetes, Obesity, Cardiovascular and Renal disease, as well as teams across Data Science, Data Engineering, AI & Digital Innovation and Global Research. You will also represent the organisation in relevant academic, biotechnology and industry collaborations. The wider geographical scope includes stakeholders in the UK, Denmark, the US and China.

**What you can expect here**

This is a player-coach opportunity for a scientific leader who wants to remain close to the work while building the capability and impact of a multidisciplinary team. You will have scope to shape scientific strategy; contribute directly to priority analyses and influence how biological evidence informs research decisions.

The role also provides opportunities to lead external collaborations, contribute to publications and conferences, and help advance the responsible use of patient and cohort data.

The Senior Supply Chain Manager, Long-Lead Equipment, is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing the end-to-end supply chain strategy for complex, long-lead materials and capital equipment across our AMERS data centre programs. This role ensures continuity of supply for critical items with extended lead times by driving rigorous forecasting, supplier collaboration, risk management, and cross-functional alignment with Engineering, Project Management, Finance, and Operations.

You will be the primary owner of long-lead equipment strategy, from early project scoping through delivery, installation, and commissioning, working within our Owner Furnished, Contractor Installed (OFCI) procurement model.

Risk Management and Mitigation  
- Identify supply, schedule, quality, and capacity risks for long-lead items and develop mitigation plans, including alternate sources, safety stock, and dual-sourcing strategies.  
- Maintain and regularly update a risk register for critical equipment and components.  
- Escalate and resolve critical issues with suppliers and internal stakeholders, ensuring clear communication and decision-making.

Process Improvement and Systems  
- Define and refine the processes, tools, and KPIs used to manage long-lead equipment across the organization.  
- Partner with IT and Systems teams to improve ERP/MRP, procurement, and tracking workflows for long-lead items.  
- Drive standardization of BOM structures, lead-time assumptions, and planning parameters to improve data quality and planning accuracy.

Cross-Functional Leadership  
- Act as the primary point of contact for long-lead equipment topics across Project Management, Engineering, Construction, and Operations.  
- Lead cross-functional reviews to align on equipment priorities, trade-offs, and decisions.  
- Mentor and support junior supply chain and procurement team members.

- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Engineering, Business, or a related field.  
- Experience in supply chain, procurement, or operations, with significant responsibility for long-lead materials or capital equipment.

Long-lead equipment is often the critical path for bringing new AI capacity online. In this role, your work directly shapes how quickly and reliably Nscale can deliver infrastructure to customers. Success will be measured by:  
- On-time delivery performance for long-lead equipment.  
- Schedule adherence for critical project milestones that depend on long-lead items.

# Full-Stack React Developer — Interactive Web Games & AI

EngineeringRemoteLong-term remote, 30–40 hours/week

## About Odeum

Odeum is building a **Narrative Learning Platform** that turns educational goals into interactive, story-driven adventures.

Teachers use **Odeum Studio** to create learning experiences with AI. Students then play those experiences directly in their web browser — exploring scenes, interacting with characters, completing quests, making choices, and learning through the story.

We're looking for a strong developer to work directly with the founder and help take ownership of the continued development of **Odeum Studio and our web-based game experience**.

This is intended to be a **long-term role**, not a short freelance project.

## What You'll Work On

You'll work across two connected parts of the product:

### Odeum Studio

Our React-based application where teachers create and edit AI-generated learning adventures.

### Web Game Runtime

The browser-based experience where students actually play those adventures.

A major part of the role will be expanding the gameplay capabilities of the web experience.

Examples of the kinds of things you may work on include:

* Character movement and animation
* Interactive objects and environments
* Scene transitions
* Dialogue and character interactions
* Quest mechanics
* Player actions and choices
* Game state and progression
* New gameplay mechanics
* Asset loading and management
* Improving game performance
* Responsive gameplay across different screen sizes

You'll also work on Studio itself, APIs, and other parts of the platform depending on your experience.

## Current Tech Stack

Our current web application uses:

* React
* TypeScript / JavaScript
* Tailwind CSS
* Zustand
* Framer Motion
* REST APIs
* AI-assisted development tools

The current game renderer uses regular HTML/CSS elements inside React.

Characters, backgrounds, and objects are rendered as positioned sprites in a scene. As our gameplay becomes more sophisticated, we may evolve the renderer or introduce technology such as:

* PixiJS
* Phaser
* Canvas / WebGL
* Three.js
* another appropriate browser game framework

We have **not predetermined the answer**.

Part of this role is helping us determine the right architecture as the product evolves.

## What We're Looking For

You should be very comfortable with:

* React
* JavaScript / TypeScript
* HTML / CSS
* Application state management
* APIs
* Git
* Debugging complex applications

We're particularly interested in developers who have built **interactive applications rather than only standard websites or CRUD applications**.

Experience with any of the following is valuable:

* PixiJS
* Phaser
* Three.js
* Canvas
* WebGL
* Browser games
* Interactive simulations
* Game development
* Animation systems

You do **not** need experience with every technology above.

We're more interested in your ability to learn quickly and solve interactive engineering problems.

## Full-Stack Experience

Backend experience is valuable but isn't required to be your strongest skill.

Our broader platform includes APIs, AI generation pipelines, and AWS infrastructure.

Experience with any of the following is a plus:

* Node.js
* REST APIs
* AWS
* S3
* DynamoDB
* Serverless applications
* AI / LLM APIs
* Structured JSON pipelines

## Bonus Skills

These are helpful but **not required**:

* Unity / C#
* Game engine architecture
* Quest or dialogue systems
* AI-generated applications
* Educational technology
* Developer tools or visual editors

## AI-Assisted Development

We actively use AI to accelerate development.

You should be comfortable using tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Lovable, or similar tools where they improve productivity.

We're not looking for someone who simply asks AI to generate code.

We're looking for someone who understands software engineering and can use AI to **build faster while maintaining good architecture and code quality**.

## What It's Like Working With Us

Odeum is an early-stage startup, so this isn't a position where you'll simply receive tickets and implement them.

You'll work directly with the founder on product and engineering decisions.

You'll have the opportunity to:

* Own significant parts of the product
* Recommend architectural improvements
* Introduce better engineering practices
* Build new gameplay systems
* Experiment with new technologies
* Help determine how our web game engine evolves

We're looking for someone who enjoys both **building things quickly** and **turning successful prototypes into reusable systems**.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone interested in a long-term relationship who can grow with the product.

## What Matters to Us

We're less interested in degrees, certifications, or knowing every technology on our list.

We care about whether you can:

**Build. Solve problems. Learn quickly. Communicate clearly. Take ownership.**

If you're a strong React developer who wants to move deeper into interactive experiences and browser game development, we'd especially like to hear from you.

## Apply for this role

Fields marked \* are required. Your resume is scanned before anyone opens it.

### Questions about this role

Please start your application with the word ODEUM in the first answer so we know you read the complete posting.

Tell us specifically what you built yourself. GitHub links, live applications, games, demos, videos, or portfolio links are all welcome.

It's completely fine if you don't have experience in every category.

For example: Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Lovable, ChatGPT, or others. Tell us briefly how you use them in your normal development workflow.

Imagine you're building a browser-based 2D experience with React and TypeScript that includes animated characters, movement, and interactive objects.
What technology or approach would you use for the interactive/game layer, and why?
A brief answer is fine — we're mainly interested in how you would approach the problem.

Staff Product Security Engineer, Offensive Security Team

This role demands more than running vulnerability scans. Excelling here requires a thorough understanding of offensive security testing and a strong drive to identify and leverage security weaknesses. This skill is key to solving security challenges, drawing on deep technical expertise and creativity.

The ideal candidate will possess demonstrable expertise in the following areas:

* **Application & Network Security:** Solid understanding of application security principles, common vulnerabilities, backend/middleware testing, and network penetration testing methodologies.

* **AI/LLM Security:** Experience assessing the security of systems that integrate large language models and AI-driven automation, including supply-chain risks in model pipelines. Ability to develop novel attack techniques against AI-augmented products and evaluate guardrail effectiveness.
* **Automation & Offensive Tooling:** A track record of building maintainable, repeatable Offensive Security tools that accelerate security assessments, automate vulnerability discovery, and integrate with existing workflows.
* **Operating Systems:** Thorough familiarity with Linux and macOS operating systems, including their security features, command-line tools, and common attack surfaces.
* **Cloud Security:** Understanding of cloud security architecture and common attack vectors. Experience with GCP is required, and depth in AWS or Azure is also welcomed.
* **Infrastructure & DevOps:** Experience with infrastructure tooling such as Kubernetes, Terraform, Chef, and ArgoCD, and an understanding of how they shape the operational environment.
* **Communication:** Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly and concisely articulate vulnerabilities and remediation strategies to technical and non-technical audiences.

We actively encourage and support the external publication of impactful security research and findings through papers, blog posts, and presentations at industry conferences.

## What You Will Do

* Apply an attacker mindset to identify, plan, and exploit complex security gaps across app, cloud, and network layers.
* Conduct targeted security assessments and pentests; deliver actionable findings, detailed exploit recreation, and architectural remediation guidance.
* Assess the security of AI/LLM-integrated features and agent-based workflows, develop novel attack techniques, and evaluate defensive controls.
* Design, build, and maintain offensive automation frameworks that scale security coverage from custom fuzzers and scanners to pipeline-integrated validation tools.
* Act as a security SME across internal teams and represent Okta in internal and external forums when appropriate.
* Periodically triage internal vulnerability tickets and external bug bounty submissions.

## What You Bring

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

We build the data processing infrastructure that underpins Palantir Foundry, supporting applications that help hospitals care for more patients, help clinical teams coordinate timely diagnoses, and keep essential supplies moving through global disruption.

You will work deep inside the systems that make this possible: how computations are represented, how query plans are optimised, how operators execute, and how data is read and written efficiently. * Java, Scala, Rust, and Python
* Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, Apache Comet, and Velox for data processing and query execution
* Apache Iceberg for table management and catalog interoperability
* Apache Arrow and Apache Parquet for in-memory data processing and columnar storage

* Eagerness to learn, ask questions, and incorporate feedback

* Strong written and verbal communication skills
* Coursework or projects in databases, compilers, operating systems, or distributed systems

# Senior Security Analyst, Security Risk Management

Security

Seattle Office, Raleigh Office, San Francisco HQ, New York City Office

Full-time

 Apply

We enable Plaid to quickly build safe and secure products while ensuring that Plaid's users, data, and infrastructure remains protected.

We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

## **About the team:**

The Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is part of Plaid’s security organization, focused on enabling the business by proactively managing information security risks and maintaining effective controls.

Our mission is to reduce the likelihood and impact of security risks while operating a robust assurance program that builds trust with our customers, consumers, and data partners.We partner closely across the company to ensure Plaid’s platform remains secure, resilient, and aligned with industry and regulatory expectations.Security risk management is how Plaid makes informed security trade-offs—we identify and analyze the risks that could materially affect the business, make sure the right owners decide what to do about them, and turn that picture into reporting leadership and the board can act on.

## **About the role:**

* You will run security risk assessments end-to-end within Plaid’s security risk management program—intake, scenario-based analysis, treatment decisions, and monitoring across security, infrastructure, and product risk.
* You will work with engineering SMEs and risk owners on risks ranging from over-privileged access and supply-chain gaps to product abuse and AI adoption, giving owners a clear, defensible basis for accepting or mitigating each one.
* You will build quarterly security risk reporting and the security risk content in leadership and board materials.
* You will help integrate security risk into enterprise risk management, so it is tracked and weighed alongside the rest of the business.
* You will help mature the program as its scope grows, and operate as an AI power user who automates the work so it scales.

## **Responsibilities:**

* **Run Security Risk Assessments:** Triage intake, run scenario-based risk analyses with engineering SMEs, score initial and residual risk, and drive risk owners to a documented treatment decision. Your analysis turns vague concerns into decisions leadership can stand behind.
* **Build Quarterly Risk Reporting:** Gather updates on material risks, prepare the Security Risk Review, and build the security risk content for executive and board decks. Your reporting gives leadership a clear, current view of where security risk sits and what’s being done about it.
* **Integrate Security Risk into ERM:** Partner with enterprise risk stakeholders to map security risks into the enterprise taxonomy, align rating scales, and keep the registers in sync. Your work puts security risk alongside business risk instead of in a silo.
* **Mature the Program:** Help evolve the risk framework, register, key risk indicators, and risk-owner self-service as the program’s scope grows. Your work moves the program from tracking risks to measuring and reducing them.
* **Support FedRAMP 20x Risk Decisions:** Help make sure unmet FedRAMP rules and KSI gaps carry a documented risk explanation and senior-official acceptance in the Security Decision Record, consistent with the risk register. Your work keeps Plaid’s FedRAMP risk posture defensible to agencies and assessors.
* **Scale Through AI and Automation:** Build AI skills and automations for intake triage, first-draft risk analyses, register hygiene, and report generation—and share them across the team. Your approach lets the program cover more risk without adding headcount.

## **Qualifications:**

Must haves:

* Security risk assessment:

  + Experience running scenario-based analyses of technical risks (cloud, IAM, software supply chain, application and product) using NIST SP 800-30, FAIR, or a comparable method.
  + Technical depth to engage engineers on architecture and controls, and to tell a real exposure from a hypothetical one.
* Risk program maturity and ERM integration:

  + Experience building or maturing a security risk program—methodology, register, treatment and exception workflow, and key risk indicators.
  + Experience integrating security risk into an enterprise risk management program.
* Risk reporting and executive communication:

  + Experience preparing quarterly risk reporting and building security risk content for executive and board decks.
  + Ability to turn technical risk into a concise executive narrative without overstating or hand-waving.
* Security and compliance knowledge:

  + Working knowledge of NIST 800-53, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and SOC 2, and how risk management feeds each.
* AI fluency and tooling:

  + Power user who has built AI skills, agents, or automations that materially increase risk-program throughput—and who shares what works with the team.

Nice to have:

* Hands-on FedRAMP 20x experience, including Security Decision Record reporting for rules and Key Security Indicators (SDR-CSO-FRR, SDR-CSX-KSI).

Our mission at Plaid is to unlock financial freedom for everyone. To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. We recognize that strong qualifications can come from both prior work experiences and lived experiences. We encourage you to apply to a role even if your experience doesn't fully match the job description. We are always looking for team members that will bring something unique to Plaid!

**Role Purpose**

The Snowflake Data/DBT Engineer is responsible for designing, developing, maintaining and optimising Plan International’s cloud-based data platform and data integration solutions. The role delivers scalable, secure, resilient and high-performing data pipelines and data products that enable trusted reporting, analytics, business intelligence and data-driven decision-making across the organisation. Working within the global Data & Analytics function, the role focuses on building and supporting modern ELT processes using Snowflake, dbt and SQL, integrating data from SAP S/4HANA and other enterprise systems into a governed enterprise data platform.

The position holder ensures that data engineering solutions are reliable, performant, well modelled, observable, secure, cost-effective and maintainable. The role contributes to data quality, governance, metadata, lineage and data security requirements and supports the continual evolution of Plan International’s modern cloud data architecture. The position holder collaborates closely with business stakeholders, Data Architects, Reporting & Analytics teams, Enterprise Architecture, IT, source-system owners and implementation partners to develop robust, reusable and maintainable data engineering solutions supporting Plan International’s global operations across more than 80 countries.

**Accountabilities**

**Snowflake Data Engineering**

* Design, develop and maintain scalable ELT pipelines using Snowflake, dbt and SQL.
* Build reusable, modular and well-tested dbt models following enterprise engineering standards.
* Develop high-performance analytical and dimensional data models that support enterprise reporting, analytics and self-service BI.
* Apply appropriate Snowflake optimisation techniques, including effective data modelling, micro-partition pruning, clustering where appropriate, warehouse sizing, workload management and query optimisation.
* Design and implement incremental processing, change data capture and historisation strategies appropriate to business and technical requirements.
* Develop reusable engineering patterns, frameworks, macros and packages to improve development efficiency and consistency.
* Implement robust error handling, monitoring, alerting and automated recovery processes within data pipelines.
* Ensure data engineering solutions are scalable, secure, resilient, maintainable and aligned with enterprise architecture standards.
* Apply appropriate Snowflake capabilities, including dynamic tables, streams, tasks and other platform services where they provide an effective solution to business requirements.

**Data Integration & ETL Development**

* Develop and support enterprise ETL/ELT solutions integrating SAP S/4HANA and other enterprise source systems into Snowflake.
* Design and maintain data ingestion and integration processes using SNP Glue and associated technologies.
* Apply appropriate integration and orchestration patterns, including scheduled, event-driven and API-based processing where required.
* Develop incremental loading, CDC and automated data validation processes.
* Investigate and resolve data integration issues across multiple platforms, source systems and environments.
* Ensure data quality, completeness, consistency and integrity throughout the data lifecycle.
* Investigate and reconcile data between SAP S/4HANA and Snowflake to identify discrepancies, data-quality issues and integration defects.
* Collaborate with source-system owners to understand data structures, business processes, source-system changes and integration requirements.
* Assess the impact of upstream system changes on downstream data pipelines and analytical datasets.
* Maintain appropriate technical documentation for source-to-target mappings, integration processes and transformation logic.

**Data Modelling & Analytics Enablement**

* Design and implement scalable dimensional and analytical data models aligned with enterprise data architecture principles.
* Apply appropriate approaches to data grain, keys, historisation, slowly changing dimensions and reusable/conformed business entities.
* Develop trusted, reusable datasets to support Power BI, Microsoft Fabric and other analytical and reporting platforms.
* Work with Reporting & Analytics teams to ensure datasets are performant, appropriately structured and fit for analytical consumption.
* Ensure transformation logic is transparent, documented and traceable from source through to consumption.
* Support the development of reusable semantic and business data structures where required.
* Ensure data models support both current reporting requirements and future analytical use cases.

**DevOps & Platform Operations**

* Support DevOps practices including CI/CD pipelines, automated deployments and source-code management.
* Maintain version-controlled dbt projects and deployment processes across development, test and production environments.
* Implement automated validation and testing as part of the development and deployment lifecycle.
* Apply appropriate unit, integration, data-quality and regression testing practices.
* Participate in release planning, deployment activities and production support.
* Contribute to Infrastructure as Code and automated provisioning practices where applicable.
* Monitor platform health, investigate incidents and implement continuous improvements to operational performance
* Develop and maintain technical documentation for engineering solutions, deployment processes and operational procedures
* Establish and maintain appropriate development, testing and production controls.

**Collaboration & Solution Delivery**

job_description:
*This project is one of a number in competition for a studentship from the Faculty of Engineering and Design at the University of Bath. If successful, this studentship is expected to commence 04 October 2027.*

*An alternative start date may be possible if agreed with your intended supervisors and the Doctoral College.*

The lead supervisor for this project will be Dr Evangelos Kallitsis, who will join the University of Bath before the project start date.

The rapid transition to electric mobility is shifting reliance from fossil fuels to mineral resources. Central to this transition are lithium-ion batteries, with a large volume expected to reach end of life over the coming decades. Sustainably managing these end-of-life flows requires recycling processes that are scalable, profitable and environmentally beneficial. In principle, recycling displaces mined materials such as lithium and cobalt and reduces environmental impacts at product level [1], and recent industrial-scale data suggest it outperforms mining supply chains [2]. However, these benefits depend strongly on battery chemistry and process configuration, and the feed to recycling plants is changing. Today's end-of-life stream is dominated by nickel- and cobalt-rich NMC cells and manufacturing scrap, but it will increasingly contain lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and sodium-ion cells with far lower metal value [3]. Plants designed now will operate for decades, yet process models and life cycle assessments (LCAs) typically evaluate one route for one fixed feed. Dynamic models are needed that can assess, and design for, this changing technological landscape. 

This PhD will develop a systems modelling framework for designing battery recycling processes under changing economic, technological and regulatory conditions, by:

- Performing dynamic material flow analysis (MFA) to forecast the volume and composition of end-of-life battery flows reaching recycling plants to 2050.

- Developing a superstructure of flowsheet options (pyrometallurgical, hydrometallurgical and direct recycling) and performing targeted process simulation to generate mass and energy balances.

- Evaluating the environmental impact and cost with LCA and techno-economic analysis (TEA) for different battery recycling scenarios at process and supply chain level.

- Using key findings to support industry decision making and to inform the regulatory landscape, such as recycled-content and recovery targets [4].

## Entry Requirements

Applicants must have, or be about to obtain, a UK Honours degree 1st or 2.1, or international equivalent. A master’s level qualification would also be advantageous.

**Non-UK applicants, who are not currently studying in the UK, must meet the programme’s** English language requirement **before the application deadline – no exceptions will be considered.**

Experience of any of the following is desirable but not essential, as training will be provided: process simulation (e.g. Aspen Plus, gPROMS), life cycle assessment, material flow analysis, techno-economic analysis, programming in Python.

## Fees

Applicants will be considered for a studentship. Studentships cover tuition fees, provide a £1k per annum training support fee, and a maintenance stipend (£21,805 2026/27 rate). International students will be required to cover the cost of a Student visa and Immigration Health Surcharge from personal funds.

Informal enquiries are encouraged. Direct these to Dr Hannah Leese - hsl25@bath.ac.uk.

Please follow the below instructions carefully.

You must make a formal application via the University of Bath’s online application form for a **PhD in Chemical Engineering**

**Please note that you can apply for a maximum of two PhD projects on this programme.**

In the ‘Funding Your Studies’ section, you must select ‘University of Bath URSA’ from one of the drop-down menus.

In the ‘Your PhD project’ section, you must quote the project title in the PhD project title field, and you must quote the lead supervisor’s name in the field ‘Name of intended supervisor at University of Bath.’

If you are applying for two projects, you must quote the project title for your second choice project in the field ‘Project 2 Title’ and the lead supervisor’s name in ‘Name of intended supervisor for 2nd choice project at University of Bath.

**You must ensure that you follow the above steps correctly. Failure to complete these steps will cause errors in the automated processing of your application and may mean that you are not considered for a particular project.**

* Real curiosity about crypto and blockchain: able to hold a credible conversation about protocols, bridges, custody, DeFi mechanics, and security risk, or a clear track record of teaching yourself a technical domain fast.

### About Us

Zodia Markets is a regulated institutional digital-asset brokerage backed by SC Ventures (the innovation and ventures arm of Standard Chartered, our majority shareholder). We provide institutional clients with stablecoin FX execution, liquidity and near-instant cross-border settlement across multiple stablecoins and 20+ fiat currencies.

Having found strong product-market fit for corporate stablecoin payments, we are now scaling that into our core focus area, underpinned by a scalable technology platform built to run it at institutional scale. As financial markets move toward always-on, programmable infrastructure, we believe institutions should be able to move capital globally with the same speed and ease as information — and we are building the regulated infrastructure to make that possible.

Today we serve banks, asset managers, hedge funds, payment providers, corporates and digital-asset institutions globally — institutional counterparties only, never retail. The team is 60 people: a mid-sized regulated financial institution, not an early-stage startup.

The Opportunity

This is the General Counsel role for a business scaling something that's already working, not a caretaker legal seat on a static book of business. Zodia is looking for a pragmatic, commercially minded lawyer who comes to the table with options, not just objections, and who wants to be closely involved in scaling our stablecoin payments strategy and the licensing, partnership and product work that goes with it.

It is a hands-on role: the successful candidate will work directly with product, engineering and commercial teams as well as the CEO and board, will be comfortable trading off legal risk against commercial outcomes rather than defaulting to the most cautious position, and will be judged on outcomes delivered — licences obtained, deals signed, structures stood up — not just advice given. The role can be based in London or Abu Dhabi, reflecting our UK and ADGM-regulated entities, or split across both.

* This is a senior appointment, and we are hiring for judgement and character at least as much as years qualified. In practice, that means candidates who have already operated at General Counsel, deputy General Counsel, or senior partner/in-house counsel level — but we'd rather meet someone with the right instincts and a slightly shorter CV than a longer CV without them.
* Qualified lawyer (solicitor or equivalent) in England & Wales, or in another relevant common-law jurisdiction with strong England & Wales-equivalent experience; an additional qualification or working fluency relevant to a UAE jurisdiction, the EU, or US/Canadian financial services law is a strong advantage given our footprint.
* A track record of having personally owned (not just supported) outcomes: at least one full regulatory licensing process taken end-to-end, significant commercial/technology or banking-partner agreements negotiated to signature, and direct experience advising a board. In-house experience in fintech, payments, digital assets or financial markets is essential.
* Direct experience leading a UK regulatory authorisation process (e.g. FCA) is highly desirable; experience with ADGM FSRA, EU MiCA/payment institution authorisation, or US/Canadian money-transmission/AML regimes is a plus.
* Demonstrated experience structuring and negotiating commercial and technology agreements, ideally including payment, custody, trading or banking-partner arrangements.
* Experience operating across multiple legal entities and jurisdictions, and coordinating with local counsel.
* Some exposure to general corporate practice — employment, data protection, corporate governance or M&A/investment — in addition to regulatory and payments work; we need a generalist who can also cover the regulatory and payments ground deeply, not a pure regulatory specialist.
* A genuine interest in, and ideally direct experience with, digital assets, stablecoins and payments infrastructure.

Skills & Personal Attributes

* Pragmatic, commercially minded and solutions-oriented — comfortable presenting options with their associated risk and reward, rather than defaulting to ‘no’.
* A demonstrated bias to action: judged by licences obtained, deals closed and structures stood up, not just risk memos issued.
* Confident operating with a good degree of autonomy in a smaller, fast-moving organisation, while exercising sound judgement about when to escalate.
* Strong drafting and negotiation skills, with an eye for the commercial substance behind the legal detail.
* A clear, persuasive communicator able to explain legal and regulatory issues to non-lawyers and help the leadership team reach decisions.
* Comfortable with ambiguity, and able to build processes and frameworks where none yet exist.
* Able to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality work to tight deadlines.
* A collaborative team player who will, over time, become an effective people leader as the legal function is built out.

Strategy & Commercial Leadership

* Act as chief legal adviser to the CEO, board and leadership team, giving pragmatic, commercially minded advice that supports business objectives — presenting options and trade-offs rather than defaulting to risk-averse positions.
* Own Zodia Markets' overall legal strategy, including entity structuring, the licensing roadmap for corporate stablecoin payments, and the legal risk appetite appropriate for a fintech business that moves client money.
* Build and lead the in-house legal function as the business scales, including recruiting, developing and managing legal team members over time.
* Act as a trusted partner to the CEO, COO, CCO, CTO/Product and Finance functions, embedding legal input early in product design and commercial negotiations rather than at the end.
* Represent Zodia Markets' legal positions with regulators, industry bodies and trade associations as required, and build the firm's thought leadership in digital-asset, payments and fintech law.

Regulatory & Licensing

* Lead Zodia Markets' licence applications and ongoing regulatory engagement, coordinating internal workstreams (Compliance, Risk, Finance, Technology) and external counsel across our regulatory footprint — UK FCA (cryptoasset registration), ADGM FSRA (Abu Dhabi), and FinCEN/FinTRAC registrations (US/Canada) — and lead the forthcoming EU expansion, including MiCA authorisation and a Payment Institution licence, as part of scaling the stablecoin payments strategy.
* Maintain a working command of the laws and regulations relevant to a multi-entity digital-asset and money-movement business, including (as applicable) FSMA, the Money Laundering Regulations, the Payment Services/E-Money Regulations, UK market conduct rules and the UK's evolving cryptoasset regime, together with the equivalent regimes in ADGM, the EU (MiCA and the Payment Services framework) and the US/Canada AML and money-transmission frameworks.
* Own the legal aspects of Zodia's multi-entity group structure, including intra-group agreements, governance documentation, and coordination with local counsel across jurisdictions.
* Monitor the external legal and regulatory environment for developments affecting digital assets, payments and financial markets, and translate them into practical guidance for the business.

Product, Commercial & Transactional

* Partner with product and engineering teams from the earliest stages of new product development — including the build-out of the scalable payments platform — understanding the technology and money-movement flows involved (custody, settlement, payment rails, trading infrastructure) and structuring products so they are both legally sound and commercially deliverable.
* Draft and negotiate commercial agreements with institutional clients, banking and payment partners, liquidity providers, custodians, and technology vendors, including IP ownership and licensing terms on platform-build contracts.
* Draft and maintain client-facing legal documentation (terms of business, account agreements, trading agreements) and intra-group services agreements.
* Select, brief and manage external counsel efficiently, balancing quality of advice against cost.
* Maintain the firm's contract repository and ensure agreements are properly executed, stored and tracked.

General Corporate, Governance & Risk

* Own company secretarial and board governance for Zodia's legal entities directly — board and committee papers, minutes, resolutions and statutory filings — rather than delegating this wholesale to external providers.
* Manage shareholder-related legal matters, including shareholder agreements, board reporting obligations and related-party arrangements arising from Zodia's ownership structure.
* Support corporate simplification activity as the group's footprint evolves, including entity disposals and licence surrenders or transfers.
* Provide or coordinate employment law support for a 60-person regulated business (contracts, policy, disciplinary and exit matters), working with HR and external employment counsel as needed.
* Own data protection and privacy compliance across jurisdictions (UK GDPR and equivalents), including cross-border data transfer arrangements suited to a multi-entity international platform.
* Manage disputes, claims and pre-litigation matters, escalating and instructing external litigation counsel where required.
* Act as an effective second-line legal risk control — providing independent, proportionate challenge on legal risk without becoming a blocker, and escalating clearly where risk appetite is exceeded, together with recommended remediation.
* Ensure appropriate legal templates, protections and remedies are in place for third-party dealings, and that Zodia's contracts are valid and enforceable under the relevant governing law.
* Provide legal input to risk and governance forums, with particular focus on product, regulatory and reputational risk.

### Role overview

Deepgram, which provides real-time APIs for speech-to-text, text-to-speech and production-grade voice agents, is hiring a Member of the Research Staff on its Voice AI Foundations effort. This full-time, employer-published remote role is listed for London, UK, and focuses on pioneering Latent Space Models (LSMs) to solve the data, scale and cost challenges of building robust, contextualized voice AI.

### Responsibilities

* Pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach aimed at the fundamental data, scale and cost challenges of building robust, contextualized voice AI.
* Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme low bit-rate compression and high-fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio.
* Pioneer steerable generative models that synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, spanning casual conversation, emotional expression and complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech.
* Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment and channel effects, enabling precise control over each aspect.
* Massively amplify existing seed datasets through latent recombination, generating synthetic audio at previously impossible scales and unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio.
* Train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that understand any human regardless of demographics, state or environment and produce empathic, human-like responses achieving conversational or task-oriented objectives.
* Design model architectures, training schemes and inference algorithms adapted for hardware at the bare metal, enabling cost-efficient training on billion-hour datasets and real-time inference for hundreds of millions of concurrent conversations.
* Focus research on solving one or more of the listed problems in codecs, generative models, embeddings, latent recombination and hardware-adapted modeling.

### Qualifications

* Strong mathematical foundation in statistical learning theory, particularly in areas relevant to self-supervised and multimodal learning.
* Deep expertise in foundation model architectures, with an understanding of how to scale training across multiple modalities.
* Proven ability to bridge theory and practice, including deriving novel mathematical formulations and implementing them efficiently.
* Demonstrated ability to build data pipelines that process and curate massive datasets while maintaining quality and diversity.
* Track record of designing controlled experiments that isolate the impact of architectural innovations and validate theoretical insights.
* Experience optimizing models for real-world deployment, including knowledge of hardware constraints and efficiency techniques.
* History of open-source contributions or research publications that have advanced the state of the art in speech/language AI.
* Active use of and experimentation with advanced AI tools, integrating AI into workflows and building AI into everyday work, per Deepgram's AI-first operating expectation.
* Comfort adopting new models and modes quickly and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.
* Willingness to work in a rapidly evolving environment where day-to-day work changes quickly, without expecting a highly prescriptive traditional 9-to-5 setup.

About the role
A hands-on analyst for a consumer energy business: pay-as-you-go cooking gas (LPG) delivered to hundreds of thousands of households in fast-growing emerging markets. You own the analysis end to end — framing the question, getting the data, building the numbers and defending them in front of the people who will act on them. You work directly with commercial, operations, finance and management, and with our founders — no account manager in between.
You join our energy data team, alongside a senior data scientist and a data & BI engineer. A meaningful part of the work starts in raw tables, meter logs, payment exports and field-operations files rather than in a tidy warehouse.
We do not require you to come from oil & gas. The business model is much closer to a prepaid mobile operator than to a fuel station: customers top up credit with mobile money, consume in small amounts, and every unit used is recorded by a smart meter. Experience at mobile network operators, telecoms, mobile money or fintech, utilities with prepaid metering, pay-as-you-go solar, and similar high-volume B2C businesses is directly relevant.


What the work looks like
Each customer home has a stove, a smart meter and a gas cylinder owned and maintained by the company. Customers pay only for the gas they use, topping up as little as a single meal’s worth through mobile money, and local technicians replace cylinders before they run out. That produces rich data — consumption, top-ups, cylinder swaps, deliveries, meter events — and commercial questions to match: which customers stay and why, what a customer is worth, where the network makes or loses money, and what to do about it.


Scope
Customer analytics — acquisition, activation, retention and churn, cohort behaviour, revenue and margin per household, lifetime value against the cost of installation
Consumption and top-up behaviour — frequency and size of top-ups, usage patterns, seasonality, early signs that a customer is about to go dormant
Pricing and promotion analysis — the effect of price, top-up incentives and campaigns on usage and margin, measured against proper baselines and control groups
Field operations and unit economics — cylinder swap and delivery efficiency, depot and area performance, technician productivity, cost to serve per household
Forecasting gas demand, cylinder logistics and revenue by area, to support supply, stock and expansion decisions
Anomaly and fraud detection — meter tampering, consumption that does not match cylinder swaps, payment irregularities, unusual field activity
Reporting with single agreed definitions where commercial, operations and finance count customers, revenue or volume differently
Messy data as the normal case: meter connectivity gaps, delayed payment records, re-assigned devices, data from more than one country and system


Requirements
4+ years as a data analyst or in a comparable analytical role, owning your own analyses from question to recommendation
Experience with high-volume B2C transactional data — prepaid mobile or telecoms, mobile money, utilities, pay-as-you-go energy, retail or similar. You know what subscriber-, account- or transaction-level data looks like and where it lies
Commercial analytics in practice: churn and retention, cohort and lifetime-value analysis, segmentation, pricing or campaign evaluation
Strong SQL and Python (pandas or similar), and readiness to work in raw data yourself: unfamiliar schemas, undocumented tables, exports never meant for analysis
Sound statistics for business questions — baselines, control groups, seasonality, telling a real effect from noise
Working with coding agents, seriously. Agents write most of the code here. Bad agent output in analysis fails silently: a join fans out rows, a filter drops half the active customers, a top-up is attributed to the wrong month. We hire for verification habits, not speed — row-count and population checks, reconciliation against a number someone already trusts, a traceable path from raw data to any figure a decision-maker sees
Experience with a BI tool (Power BI, Tableau, Metabase, Superset or similar)
Clear communication: you can explain a result, its limits and what to do about it to a non-technical manager
English sufficient to present findings and defend methodology
Professional proficiency in Russian

Experience with experimentation or A/B testing at scale

Why choose to work at Recycleye? Our team works together to grow and succeed, driven by our shared values of ambition, curiosity, customer centricity, integrity and respectful ideation. We offer great benefits, built-in upskilling and unlimited holiday. 

We know that our mission will be achieved by having the most passionate, driven, talented, and all-around best people on our team. So come and help us shape the future! 

**What you'll work on** 

Our team develops new features across Recycleye’s waste sorting and plant monitoring products, improving the end-to-end performance of our systems. That might mean evaluating and deploying new model architectures, adapting ideas from ML papers to our use cases, implementing novel object tracking algorithms, diving deep into camera optics and calibration, or making our DeepStream pipelines more efficient. Everything we build runs in production on real sorting lines, so we look for the solution that works best for the problem, which might mean stepping back and choosing a better camera rather than chasing a cool new model. 

You will be a core member of a small, high-impact ML R&D team. Building new features and developing better ways to measure how well our products perform, whether that’s sorting a waste stream or understanding what’s in it, and how real site conditions affect that performance. You will work closely with our data team, who train models day to day for client projects and rely on the tools we build, and with colleagues developing a new plant monitoring product. You will also help support our deployed systems and spend time on site, getting hands-on with the waste they sort. 

As the team develops, you will help shape how we work, from code review to testing, and take on more responsibility for planning and decision-making. Along the way you will build a deep understanding of our products and the waste sorting industry, keep up with advances in computer vision, and share what we learn across the company. 

We work mostly in Python, with some Go, deploying models and algorithms to NVIDIA Jetson devices running DeepStream pipelines, supported by Docker, GitHub Actions and Azure. 

**What success looks like** 

* Your work regularly reaches production and makes a measurable difference to how our products perform.

* You bring new ideas to the table, test them, and help shape what we build next.

* You grow into owning technical areas of our systems, and become a trusted reviewer and planning partner for the team.

* Teams across the company, from data to install and support, know to come to you, and you help them get the best from our systems.

* Our ways of working and measuring performance keep improving, so that our systems get better with every deployment.

We’re looking for someone who is proactive, driven and practical, comfortable with change, and keen to learn. We don’t expect you to be an expert in everything on day one. 

* Hands-on computer vision experience, with a background in ML, physics, maths, engineering or computer science.

* Around 3-5 years’ experience writing production-quality code, primarily in Python, and promoting good engineering practice.

* A track record of shipping ML into production in a commercial setting, ideally including computer vision on edge devices.

* Solid software engineering fundamentals: tested code, version control and code review.

* Clear communication with both technical and non-technical colleagues, and a collaborative approach.

* Comfort working independently and as part of a small team.

* Creative, practical problem solving.

* A love of seeing your work in the real world. You’ll spend time on site and at our demo centre, testing in challenging environments and getting hands-on with the waste our systems sort. It’s the best way to understand the problem you’re solving.

**Nice to have**

* **Models:** computer vision detector-classifier models (YOLO, RF-DETR), segmentation models

* **Algorithms**: multi-object tracking, camera calibration, homography transforms

# Software Engineer - Localisation

London, United Kingdom

# **About ROLLER**

ROLLER isn’t your average SaaS company. We operate globally across 30+ countries, powering millions of real-world experiences in the leisure and attractions industry. What we build doesn’t just live on a screen. It shows up in busy venues, peak weekends, and unforgettable moments for guests.

Our mission is simple but ambitious: help operators run better businesses while creating great guest experiences. That means solving complex, real-world problems across ticketing, point of sale, self-service, memberships, kiosks, and digital waivers, all at meaningful scale.

Just as importantly, it’s the people. We’re a team of 300+ smart, grounded, and genuinely passionate humans working across the globe. We care about quality, ownership, and doing work we’re proud of, without taking ourselves too seriously.

We’re growing fast, aiming high, and building something that matters. If you want to work on real problems, with real customers, alongside people who care deeply about their craft and impact, ROLLER is a great place to do it.

# **Why You’ll Enjoy This Role!**

🚀  **Work that keeps venues trading -** You’ll own fiscal and regulatory compliance across Europe. If it’s wrong, a venue can’t legally trade, so getting it right matters.

🤝  **Your squad owns it -** Squads are self-managing. The London squad owns localisation and compliance for Europe end to end, and you’ll work with your PM to decide what gets built, how it’s built and when it ships.

🌍  **Real scale, real consequences -** Thousands of requests per second across hundreds of containers, powering over 100 million guest experiences in 2025 alone.

✨  **Help shape a growing team -** Be one of the first engineers in London, set how the squad works, and help new engineers get up to speed.

# **Why This Role Matters**

ROLLER is growing fast across Europe, and every new market brings its own rules on tax, invoicing, receipts and language. Our London squad makes sure venues in those markets can trade legally and run in their own language. Recent work includes fiscal compliance for markets like France, Germany and Austria, and AI-assisted translations across the platform.

You’ll join a small London squad reporting to a London based Tech Lead. Our HQ is in Australia, so most of your work with the wider team is async, with live time together every week or two. You’ll be comfortable owning your work, unblocking yourself and finding your own ways to stay connected.

Our backend runs on C#, .NET, T-SQL and AWS services including Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, S3, SES and SQS. On the front end, we use Angular alongside our own design system and component library.

# **What You’ll Do**

**Build**

* Design, build and ship changes across backend services, APIs and the Angular interfaces venues use every day
* Build patterns for regional rules and compliance that we can extend to new markets

**Own integrations**

* Lead integration-heavy work with third-party providers, like fiscal and certification partners: define the contract, handle the edge cases and plan for failure
* Work directly with those providers when something needs chasing or clarifying

**Own production**

* Collaborate closely with the SRE team to monitor system performance and proactively identify potential issues
* Triage compliance alerts and fix the root cause

**Raise the bar**

* Share what you know through code reviews, pairing and honest feedback
* Work with your PM to break vague regulatory requirements into small, shippable pieces

# **About You**

* You have a high appetite for Technology and AI and a natural curiosity for how it can transform your work. You’re comfortable using AI tools to automate repetitive 'busy work,' freeing you up to focus on high-impact work.
* Solid mid-level or senior experience building and shipping full-stack software in a SaaS product company
* Deep backend experience in C# and .NET, and enough Angular or TypeScript to work across the stack
* Deep knowledge of cloud patterns, application and database performance, with experience applying them to varying workflows and workloads
* You’ve built integrations with third-party systems where the details matter: payments, tax, invoicing, compliance or similar
* You can take a vague requirement, like a new country’s tax rules, and turn it into something shipped
* You do your best work async: you write things down clearly, unblock yourself and don’t need constant check-ins

Bonus points for experience with European fiscal rules, or for speaking French or German. You don’t need to match every point.

We believe AI is a career-defining inflection point. ROLLER is a fast adopter of new technology like AI, and every team member is empowered to own their learning and use the latest tools to supercharge their impact. We’re looking for candidates with the proficiency and curiosity to embrace AI and technology, not just as a technical skill, but as a core competency to help us achieve big goals. Our engineers use Claude and other AI coding tools day to day.

# **Perks!**

🚀  You get to work on a category-leading product that customers love in a fun, high-growth industry - check our Capterra and G2 reviews.

🏥  Private medical insurance through Vitality, plus dental cover.

💷  Company pension.

🛡️  Life insurance at 4x your base salary.

💙  Team member Assistance Program to proactively support our team’s health and wellbeing - access to coaching, education modules, weekly webinars, and more.

🍼  16 weeks paid Parental Leave for primary carers and 4 weeks paid Parental Leave for secondary carers

🎉  Engage in our ‘Vibe Tribe’ - led by our team members; you can contribute to company-wide initiatives directly. Regular events and social activities, fundraising & cause-related campaigns... you name it. We’re willing to make it happen!

💡  Work with a driven, fun, and switched-on team that likes to raise the bar in all we do.

Go on, hit apply. Let’s build great tech together. If you’ve got questions, don’t be afraid to reach out to Reuben at reuben.jamieson@rollerdigital.com.

**We're building the UK's next generation engineering powerhouse, providing critical technology that strengthens national security and resilience.**

Rowden already has an excellent systems engineering team, and we already integrate, test and verify complex edge systems. However, the scale, pace and complexity of what we need to prove is changing, and with it our demand for a rigorous, end-to-end verification & validation (V&V) capability.

Our systems bring together software, compute, networks, radios, sensors, user devices and increasingly autonomous behaviour. They have to work across denied, degraded, intermittent and low bandwidth networks, where system behaviour shifts as connectivity and available resources shift. Executed well, this will significantly speed up the time it takes to get technology into users' hands - and give us confidence it will actually work for them when it gets there.
