**About Salary Finance**

Working with employers, we provide a financial wellbeing platform as an employee benefit, helping employees to understand their money better, get out of debt faster and save for their future. We already have a reach of circa 4,000,000 employees through our relationships with over 500 of the largest employers in the UK.

By improving employee financial wellbeing, we have a very real and meaningful impact on people’s lives. We remove the stress and worry associated with financial difficulties by dramatically reducing the interest rates employees pay on their personal debt, and provide them with the tools needed to start saving sooner and be more financially secure. We are backed by some of the biggest brands, including investments from Blenheim Chalcot (the UK’s leading venture builder), Legal and General (the FTSE 100 insurer and asset manager), Experian and Goldman Sachs, and funding partnerships with JP Morgan and Blue Owl.

Launched in 2015, we have made excellent progress, and are scaling fast. We have been named BITC’s Responsible Business of Year, included in KPMG’s Global Fintech 100, listed top of the Forbes' list of socially-responsible startups, and profiled by the Financial Times, the Times, the Wall Street Journal, the Guardian, the Telegraph, CityAM and the Institute of Directors.

**Your role in our mission**

As Head of Product for Borrow, you'll own our lending products from the moment a customer starts an application to the day their loan is repaid. You'll lead two product squads: one covering everything up to the point the money is paid out, and one covering everything after it. You’ll be accountable for helping more employees borrow with us, and for making sure every loan is run accurately and fairly, with customers well supported from application to final repayment. You'll report to the Product Director.

**How Borrow works**

We lend to employees through their employer. Three parties are involved:

* **Customers** are employees who take out a loan with us.
* **Employers** deduct repayments from pay and give us the data we need to confirm customers are who they say they are.
* **Salary Finance** is the lender, responsible for the application, the payout and the life of the loan.

Taking repayments straight from salary means much lower credit losses than other lenders, and we pass that saving on to customers as a lower rate. It also makes lending harder to run. Repayments follow payroll, so loans are repaid weekly, fortnightly, four-weekly or monthly. Customers can change payroll at any time. Employers pay us in bulk, and we reconcile each payment to individual loans.

**What you'll own**

**Before payout**

* Growth in applications and originations across direct, aggregator and returning-customer channels
* The application journey and its conversion across each of these channels
* Our range of lending products, including personal loans, top-up loans and debt consolidation, plus exploring opportunities such as open banking in underwriting

**After payout**

* The customer’s experience after payout; seeing their balance, making repayments, settling early and getting help, in the app and online
* Our Loan Engine; so every customer’s interest, payments and balance are right
* Regulatory documents; from credit agreements to notices of default, accurate and automated, so customers always know where they stand
* Support for customers who fall behind; from early contact and self-service through to forbearance, collections and debt sale

**What you’ll do**

* **Set the direction:** shape the Borrow product strategy and roadmap in line with company objectives with the Product Director and CPO - framed as customer and commercial outcomes to move rather than features to ship
* **Be the voice of the customer:** use customer client and colleague feedback alongside the data, so improvements reach the people who use and buy our products
* **Improve the journey:** make sure your teams are always finding and testing ways to improve the customer’s experience, from conversion through to managing and repaying their loan
* **Lead the team:** develop the team (including both Product Managers and Product Design), giving them clear outcomes and the room to own how they get there. Coach them on how they decide what to build, not only how they deliver it
* **Measure what matters:** make sure the tooling and reporting exist to measure every product, track commercial and customer outcomes, run experiments and, and make decisions on the evidence
* **Make trade-off decisions:** use evidence of what will move the outcome to decide what to do and what not to do. When there is more demand than capacity, make the choice explicit and agree it with the business before delivery starts
* **Work across the business:** partner with stakeholders across the business, from Credit Risk and Compliance to Finance and Engineering, so that products land on time, to quality and within regulatory boundaries
* **Get compliance right:** make sure customers receive the correct regulatory communications on time, every time, and own the evidence that Borrow delivers good outcomes and fair value under Consumer Duty
* **Represent Borrow:** prepare and present Borrow papers for our Product Oversight Committee

**About you**

* **Consumer lending experience:** significant product leadership in UK consumer lending, in a regulated business. This is essential.
* **Customer-obsessed:** you talk to customers and clients regularly, run research yourself, and can point to decisions you changed, and things you decided not to build, because of what you heard. You know many borrowers are under financial pressure, and you design for good outcomes as well as conversion
* **A leader of product managers:** you have led Product Managers and grown their capability, and you lead through them
* **Data-driven:** you can find the answer in a conversion funnel or a loan book yourself. You write SQL and you are quick in Excel.
* **Lending and regulation:** you know how a loan works underneath, from interest and repayment schedules to arrears and forbearance, and the FCA rules around it, including the Consumer Credit Act, CONC and Consumer Duty. You know which regulatory communications customers must receive and when, and why every calculation and letter has to be right
* **Operationally minded:** you design processes that scale, run efficiently and stay compliant
* **A clear communicator:** concise in writing and in the room, with audiences from engineers to the board
* **Comfortable with tension and ambiguity:** you can own a growth target and a control environment at the same time, make the call when the answer isn’t clear, and change course when the evidence or a better argument says so
* **Technically fluent:** you can hold your own with engineers on architecture and root causes, and they trust your judgement on trade-offs

* **AI-fluent:** you use AI tools every day to speed up analysis, discovery and writing, you help your team do the same, and you know where human checks matter most, especially on calculations and anything customer-facing

**Nice to have**

* Have led a loan servicing rebuild or a loan book migration from the product side

* Have worked with aggregators or price comparison sites

We embrace our differences but there’s one thing we like to share - our values, so it’s important to us that you are:

* **Responsible**, and want to help build a business that delivers a meaningful difference to society.

## Job Description

### Overview

As a Lead ML/AI Platform Engineer at SavvyMoney, you will own the platform that takes machine learning from experiment to production — training infrastructure, model serving, inference pipelines, and the integration seams with our Java microservices.

You will set technical direction for AI/ML across the company alongside our Data Platform Architect, and drive the engineering side of our GenAI/LLM and agent strategy — from retrieval architectures and evaluation harnesses to the guardrails required to run agentic workflows responsibly in a regulated environment.

## What You'll Do

* Partner with our Data Platform Architect to set technical direction for AI/ML across the company — architecture, tooling, standards, and build-vs-buy decisions.
* Own the ML/AI platform: training infrastructure, model serving, inference pipelines, and production integration.

  + Feature engineering, model training, model registry, and hosted inference in Amazon SageMaker
  + GenAI/LLM usage, fine-tuning, and agentic workflows in Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore
  + Feedback and data pipelines built on AWS Glue, Lambda, and Step Functions
* Own the serving layer and integrate ML services cleanly with our Java microservices — define the API contracts and make the latency and throughput trade-offs.
* Drive the engineering side of our GenAI/LLM strategy: retrieval architectures, evaluation harnesses, serving patterns, and the judgment calls about which approach fits which problem.
* Bring depth on the emerging agent stack — MCP, agent workflow patterns, stateless and stateful designs, and the guardrails needed to run them responsibly in a regulated environment.
* Partner with our Data Scientist on the handoff from experimentation to production: productionize models, stand up the feature pipelines and serving infrastructure they need, and shorten the loop between training and deployment.
* Work with product, data, and engineering leadership to identify the highest-impact ML opportunities and translate them into roadmaps.
* Represent the AI/ML function in cross-functional forums, communicating trade-offs clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.

## What We're Looking For

**Required**

* 8+ years in software or ML engineering, including 5+ years shipping production ML systems and a track record of owning ambiguous, high-scope problems end to end.
* Demonstrated technical leadership: you've shaped the ML strategy of a team or organization, mentored senior engineers, and been the person others rely on for difficult architectural calls.
* Hands-on experience with both operating models we use:

  + **AWS managed ML stack:** Amazon SageMaker (training, tuning, hosted endpoints, model registry), Amazon Bedrock, and AgentCore for GenAI and agentic workflows.
  + **Open-source ML tooling:** JupyterLab for notebooks, Spark for distributed processing, MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry.
* Deep working knowledge of the AWS stack — S3, Athena, Redshift, Glue, Step Functions, Lambda — plus SQL skills strong enough to model data for both analytical and ML workloads.
* Production experience with GenAI/LLMs: RAG, prompt engineering, evaluation, and a clear grasp of the cost, latency, and safety trade-offs involved.
* Familiarity with vector databases (e.g., pgvector, Pinecone) and sound judgment on when they're warranted versus alternatives such as NoSQL retrieval.
* Working knowledge of Java sufficient to review service code, define API contracts, and debug integration issues with our microservices.
* Deep expertise in Python and the core ML stack: scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy, PyTorch and/or TensorFlow, XGBoost / LightGBM.
* Solid MLOps fundamentals — model monitoring, drift detection, reproducibility, experiment tracking, model registry, and cost observability — plus the ability to partner with DevOps on CI/CD rather than build it from scratch.
* Excellent written and verbal communication — you can write both the design doc that aligns a dozen engineers and the one-pager that aligns the exec team.
* Strong collaborator, comfortable operating in a role where scope is shared: you'll partner with a Data Scientist on models and DevOps on infrastructure, and you can navigate those seams while keeping clear ownership.
* Ability to operate as an independent contractor through your own entity or an approved contracting arrangement, with reliable overlap with US Pacific business hours for architecture reviews and cross-team work.

**Nice to Have**

* Experience with ClickHouse or a comparable columnar / real-time analytical database.
* Fine-tuning experience (LoRA / QLoRA, instruction tuning, or RLHF).
* Streaming and real-time inference experience (Kafka, Kinesis, low-latency serving).
* Infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, AWS CDK, CloudFormation).
* Experience operating ML systems at meaningful scale — hundreds of millions of predictions per day, or equivalent.
* Open-source contributions, conference talks, papers, or patents in ML / applied ML.

## Who You'll Work With

* **Data Scientist** — leads feature engineering, model training, fine-tuning, and experimentation. You'll partner on the research-to-production handoff, stand up the infrastructure they need, and jointly own the quality of what ships.
* **DevOps** — owns CI/CD, deployment infrastructure, and platform observability. You'll partner on ML-specific extensions (model artifacts, reproducible environments, canary and shadow deployments) rather than rebuilding what already exists.
* **Backend engineers** — own the Java microservices that consume ML outputs. You'll define the contracts and own the serving side.
* **Product and engineering leadership** — you're the technical voice on what we should build with AI/ML, and how.

## Our Stack

* **Distributed processing:** AWS Glue
* **Orchestration:** AWS Lambda, AWS Step Functions
* **Managed ML:** Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore
* **Open-source ML:** JupyterLab, Spark, MLflow
* **Storage & query:** Amazon S3 (data lake), Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, ClickHouse
* **Languages:** Python (ML, pipelines), Java (microservices)  
    
  **Why This Role Matters**

  Credit data is the core of what we do, and the opportunity to make it smarter — better offer targeting, better personalization, better insight for 1,600+ financial institutions and the consumers they serve — runs directly through the ML platform. Today that platform is early. You will be the person who defines what it becomes.

  Your decisions on architecture, tooling, and evaluation will set the ceiling on what every ML-driven feature at SavvyMoney can do for years.

  Join us at SavvyMoney and help build the AI foundation of a platform trusted by 1,600+ banks and credit unions.

    As a Children's Residential Support Worker, you'll play a vital role in helping children and young people overcome challenges and achieve positive outcomes.

    You will:

    * Build positive, trusting relationships with children and young people.
    * Provide day-to-day care, guidance, and emotional support.

    * Respond calmly, confidently, and therapeutically to challenging situations.
    * Work collaboratively with colleagues, social workers, education professionals, and clinicians.
    * Contribute to care planning, record keeping, and celebrating children's achievements.

    No two days are the same, but every day offers the opportunity to make a genuine difference.

    ### About Our Bicester Home

    Our home in Bicester provides a safe, nurturing, and therapeutic environment for children and young people with complex emotional and behavioural needs.

    Situated in the heart of Oxfordshire, the home benefits from excellent access to local amenities, education providers, leisure facilities, and community resources, helping children engage in positive experiences and build meaningful connections within their local community.

    Our dedicated team is committed to providing high-quality, trauma-informed care that helps children feel safe, develop resilience, and achieve positive outcomes tailored to their individual needs and aspirations.

    ## What We're Looking For

    We're looking for resilient, compassionate individuals who understand that behaviour is often a communication of unmet need.

    You'll need:

    * Experience working with children, young people, or adults with complex needs, emotional and behavioural difficulties, or behaviours that challenge.
    * Strong emotional resilience and the ability to remain calm under pressure.
    * Confidence managing difficult situations using therapeutic and child-centred approaches.
    * Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
    * A genuine passion for helping children achieve positive outcomes.
    * A full UK driving licence.
    * Flexibility to work shifts, weekends, bank holidays, and sleep-ins.
    * A willingness to complete a Level 3 Diploma in Residential Childcare if not already qualified.

    Most importantly, we're looking for people who can see beyond behaviour and recognise the experiences, emotions, and unmet needs behind it.

    ## What We Offer

    * Salary of £29,767 - £31,579 per annum (£14.31 - £15.18 per hour).
    * £50.00 per sleep-in.
    * Ofsted Bonus Scheme for homes achieving Good or Outstanding inspection outcomes.
    * Annual Attendance Bonus.
    * Enhanced Family Friendly Leave.
    * Award and Recognition Vouchers celebrating outstanding achievements and contributions.
    * Comprehensive induction and specialist training.
    * Fully funded Level 3 Diploma in Residential Childcare.
    * Clinical support through our Homes & Horizons therapeutic model.
    * Career progression opportunities within a growing national organisation.
    * 28 days annual leave, increasing with service.
    * Free meals whilst on shift.
    * Unum Healthcare, providing healthcare reimbursements, remote GP access, wellbeing resources, and mental health support.
    * Aviva Digicare, including Digital GP consultations, annual health checks, and mental health assessments.
    * Employee discounts on shopping, cinema, travel, and holidays.
    * Blue Light Card eligibility.
    * Cycle to Work Scheme.
    * Access to confidential counselling and wellbeing support through our Employee Assistance Programme.
    * Christmas recognition vouchers and long-service awards.
    * Ongoing support, learning, and development opportunities.

    ## Important Information

    All successful candidates will be subject to pre-employment safer recruitment checks in line with Ofsted regulatory requirements and the Homes2Inspire Safer Recruitment Policy.

    We are unable to offer sponsorship for this role.

    Applications will be reviewed regularly, and we reserve the right to interview and appoint before the advertised closing date.

    Interviews for this role will take place in person during planned assessment days. Please contact our Careers Team if you require any reasonable adjustments.

On occasion, this may result in an offer being made for an alternative service to the one originally applied for.

    At Homes2Inspire, we're committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace where everyone feels valued, respected, and supported.

    We actively encourage applications from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic communities and welcome applications from all sections of society, including people with lived experience of disability, social exclusion, or care experience.

    Homes2Inspire is proud to support care leavers through our Guaranteed Interview Scheme. If you have lived experience of care and meet the minimum criteria for the role, please tell us as part of your application.

# Integrated Photonics Engineer/Senior Integrated Photonics Engineer

Bristol-based health tech start-up Siloton seeks a skilled and innovative technical lead who is interested in applying their photonics engineering skills to improve the lives of people with eye disease.

Role overview:

* In-person position (hybrid options available).
* Full-time preferred, part-time applications considered.
* Core role as part of an interdisciplinary technical team
* Must have the right to work in the UK.
* Starting as soon as possible

## What we do

Four hundred and twenty million people suffer from chronic eye disease; it is the leading cause of sight loss in the developed world. To prevent people going blind, clinicians take sub-surface images of the back of the eye so that the condition can be diagnosed and managed appropriately. This uses a device called an optical coherence tomography machine, or ‘OCT’, which currently require bulky, desk-sized workstations. Siloton is developing the first truly portable OCT to provide better access to diagnostic and monitoring services for everyone who needs it. Based on Siloton’s world-leading photonic chip technology, this will reduce the burden of treatment while removing bottlenecks in the clinical pipeline, alleviating pressure on healthcare systems and ensuring patients receive the best possible care, wherever and whoever they are.

## What we are looking for

Your role will be to work on the development of core integrated photonic capabilities as part of the dedicated and passionate engineering team of photonic, hardware, and software specialists working to create the next generation of retinal scanning device. The chip projects as part of this role will feed into a larger set of development goals leading towards direct imaging of patients and development of a device for clinical trials.

This is a wide-ranging technical role, covering many aspects of integrated photonics, with a diverse and interesting set of problems to solve. Your primary responsibilities will be to work with the CTO to complete the design, development, and implementation of photonic chips fundamental to prototype development and patient imaging. This includes but is not limited to:

1. Simulating and designing photonic integrated circuit (PICs) components using FDTD packages such as Lumerical or similar suites
2. Completing layout of PICs at both multi-project wafer and full-wafer scale using GDS Factory, Nazca, or similar software
3. Testing, characterising, and demonstrating the functionality of existing and new photonic chip devices, including imaging via in-vivo and patient trials
4. Constructing and demonstrating prototype imaging devices incorporating photonic chips
5. Assembly, testing, and installation of commercial (pre-regulated) devices to customers
6. Establishing alignment/characterisation/assembly/manufacturing procedures as we move towards product launch
7. IP generation and protection, including patent writing
8. Liaising with collaborators, suppliers, and customers where required

Supplementary to this, there are additional opportunities to get involved with other work at Siloton based on personal interest, including but not limited to:

1. A chance to engage and do technical development with our academic and clinical partners and advisors
2. Providing technical input to business and customer development
3. Direct experience with investor and fundraising activities
4. Developing technology under a medical device quality management system (ISO-13485)
5. Working with a broader team to develop technology for assessment in a formal clinical trial

The position includes the opportunity to gain experience in, and exposure to, many areas of integrated photonic design and implementation from core design and development through to direct user engagement (patient imaging). The role will have a primary focus on photonic chip engineering and demonstrations with the Siloton system, including integration and work with the wider electronic, photonic, and software systems. There will be opportunities for mentorship and training through both internal and external personnel.

# Senior Product Manager, Data Platform - PDEGO

London

## **About Sony Music Entertainment**

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Today, we work in more than 70 countries, supporting a diverse roster of international superstars, developing and independent artists, and visionary creators. From our position at the intersection of music, entertainment, and technology, we bring imagination and expertise to the newest products and platforms, embrace new business models, employ breakthrough tools, and provide powerful insights that help our artists push creative boundaries and reach new audiences. In everything we do, we’re committed to artistic integrity, transparency, and entrepreneurship.

Sony Music Entertainment is a member of the Sony family of global companies.

Sony Music is looking for a **Senior Product Manager, Data** to join our talented product team in our London office and lead the development of a portfolio of shared data products.

Our products and teams work with data spanning streaming, fan engagement, social and creator activity, and commerce. As new datasets and requirements emerge, we need to understand what the data contains, establish what it means and make it useful beyond the team or product where it originated.

You will own the strategy, roadmap and delivery of a portfolio of shared data products. Working with business stakeholders, source-product owners and data engineering, you will turn business needs into clear requirements, deliver dependable datasets and establish definitions and relationships that can be reused across products.

## **What you’ll do:**

* **Own the strategy and roadmap for a portfolio of shared data products, with a focus on developing new datasets to meet emerging business needs.** Understand needs across teams, identify valuable opportunities and prioritise a portfolio of initiatives that supports artist teams and the wider business.
* **Turn business requests into well-defined data initiatives.** Meet the people who produce and use the data, examine source datasets and establish the questions users need to answer, the information required and the measures of success.
* **Define reusable datasets with engineering.** Agree on the records, fields, relationships, quality, freshness and access requirements needed for each use case you’re defining. Establish clear acceptance criteria and resolve tradeoffs with stakeholders and engineers.
* **Lead delivery and adoption.** Maintain a prioritised backlog and work with engineering through implementation, validation, launch and ongoing improvement. Ensure the teams receiving the data can use it to meet the agreed need.
* **Steward shared definitions and data models.** Work with domain experts and engineers to establish consistent definitions, identifiers, relationships and metrics. Develop the shared semantic layer through the initiatives you deliver, so concepts such as artists, tracks, markets, campaigns and audiences can be understood consistently across products.
* **Connect datasets to enable new capabilities.** Identify where combining data creates value and lead the product work required, including opportunities to relate streaming performance to social activity, campaigns, fan engagement and commerce.
* **Make data discoverable and understandable.** Ensure data products have clear documentation, usage examples and known limitations, helping analysts, data scientists and downstream product teams use them confidently.
* **Help develop and apply practical data standards.** Partner with leadership, engineering and relevant specialists on quality, ownership, access, lineage and appropriate use. Translate these expectations into requirements for the data products you lead.
* **Agree responsibilities for ongoing use of the data products you deliver.** Work with source-product owners and engineering teams to establish how source changes, maintenance, quality issues and communication with users will be handled for those initiatives.
* **Measure adoption and impact.** Gather user feedback and evidence of usefulness, track whether the capabilities delivered meet their intended outcomes and use those findings to inform the roadmap.
* **Build stakeholder alignment.** Explain priorities and investment decisions, communicate progress and translate technical considerations into clear business implications.

You will work closely with our existing Data Platform product and engineering teams, coordinating priorities and dependencies with the platform migration and operational roadmap. You will also partner with source-product PMs and the teams building on the shared data products you deliver.

About the role
We're hiring our first dedicated product designer, full-time, to shape Spate's core product: the dashboard where brand teams explore trends, build reports, and work with our AI assistant.
Our platform will change a lot over the next year or two as we rebuild around LLM-powered features. We already ship an AI Assistant, AI Reports (an LLM-powered dashboard builder), and in-dashboard summaries and analysis. We need someone who can work out what those experiences should be, not just how they should look.
Our users are brand innovation teams, product marketers, social media teams, and agencies. Most aren't data analysts, so much of the job is turning dense trend data into something clear and actionable.

The product, not just the screens. At Spate, product design and UI/UX design happen together. Features aren't fully defined and then handed to a designer. You'll help decide what we build and why, and stay involved from the first conversation to launch. You'll work with our frontend lead to choose the right deliverable for each problem: a written proposal, a user flow, a prototype, or a full Figma spec.
Finding problems worth solving. Find user pain points on your own, through customer calls, interviews, feedback, and usage data. Then take them from problem to proposal: frame the problem, explore options, and make the case for a direction. Leadership sets the overall direction and can help point you at problems, but you won't need our input to get started.
How our AI features work. Decide when something should be a chat, a report, or an inline summary. Define how we show where an insight came from, and how we handle loading, uncertainty, and wrong answers. Help shape the voice and structure of AI-generated insights, because in an LLM product the words are part of the UX.
The design system. We have a Figma library and a React component library that are only loosely in sync. You'll own the system's principles and the Figma side, and partner with our frontend engineers to make the two a single source of truth. The goal is that everyday design decisions are answered by the system, so engineers can ship UI that feels like Spate without waiting on design. This includes data visualization standards and patterns for AI features.
The feedback loop, with our frontend lead. Co-own product metrics, user feedback tracking, and quality evaluation for our LLM features. A big part of this is defining what a good AI answer looks like for our users, and turning that into rubrics we can measure.

Contributors at Spate work flexibly, with few meetings, a lot of impact, and real say over the direction of their work. Leadership sets product direction and priorities, and you shape how we get there. That means bringing proposals rather than waiting for briefs.

We're building the infrastructure layer for agentic web interaction at scale. Our API is designed from the ground up to power Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and real-time reasoning in AI systems. By connecting LLMs to high-quality, trustworthy web content, we help developers build agents that are not only intelligent — but also informed. 

We work with some of the most innovative teams in AI — from small startups shaping the ecosystem to the largest enterprises deploying AI at scale. Whether it's powering sales assistants, research copilots, or internal knowledge tools, we're the missing link between LLMs and the real world.

You will build browser infrastructure and tooling that enables reliable, efficient access to web content across a rapidly changing web.

**About Telnyx**

*Telnyx is an industry leader that's not just imagining the future of global connectivity—we're building it. *We're driven by a desire to transform and modernize what's antiquated, automate the manual, and solve real-world problems through innovative connectivity solutions. As a testament to our success, we're proud to stand as a financially stable and profitable company. Our robust profitability allows us not only to invest in pioneering technologies but also to foster an environment of continuous learning and growth for our team.*

*Our collective vision is a world where borderless connectivity fuels limitless innovation. By joining us, you can be part of laying the foundations for this interconnected future. We're currently seeking passionate individuals who are excited about the opportunity to contribute to an industry-shaping company while growing their own skills and careers.*

#### 

#### The opportunity

We're looking for a Director or VP of Enterprise Sales to build and lead our direct enterprise business across Europe. This is distinct from our ISV and platform sales motion. The mandate is to win major European enterprises, create a focused regional playbook and build the organization to scale it. We'll calibrate the title to the leader's experience and scope.

Europe's largest enterprises are moving more communications and customer workflows into software and AI, but they face real constraints around data residency, telecom requirements, legacy systems, procurement and cross-border operations. They need partners that understand where infrastructure runs, how it connects, what it costs and how to deploy reliably in production.

Telnyx has an unusual platform for those conversations: its own network and communications stack, integrated with AI and inference capabilities. The opportunity is to make that technical differentiation relevant to the buying priorities of European multinationals, prove it in initial deployments and expand into durable enterprise relationships.

#### What you'll build

* A European enterprise organization. Build an initial team of eight enterprise account executives, paired one-to-one with field development engineers (FDEs). Establish the pod model, hiring bar, management cadence and shared technical-sales accountability. Scale toward 16 sellers only when repeatable performance supports it.
* A deliberate country and account plan. Prioritize markets and industries based on addressable revenue, readiness to buy, competitive advantage and our ability to serve customers well. Start with a named-account strategy then segment for scale across Europe.
* A disciplined multinational sales motion. Build relationships with country operators and central buying groups, navigate local and global stakeholders, and manage complex security, legal and procurement processes. Know when a local use case can become an enterprise-wide standard.
* Technically credible solution selling. Lead with the customer's operational and economic problem, then prove the architecture with FDEs through demos, technical validation, integrations and production pilots. Be precise about network performance, AI inference, data handling, security and deployment requirements.
* Repeatable commercial plays. Package wins in customer engagement, contact centers, AI agents, programmable voice and messaging, real-time network services and AI infrastructure into examples the team can take across similar European accounts. Work with Product and Marketing on localized customer proof and industry narratives where they matter.
* An operating system for profitable growth. Own pipeline generation, forecasting, territory design, conversion, rep productivity, hiring, coaching and deal inspection. Partner closely with Marketing, Product, RevOps and Customer Success, and coordinate with our other regional and ISV teams on account ownership and expansion.

#### How we'll measure success

The ultimate scorecard is revenue. We will measure net-new European enterprise ARR, qualified pipeline, win rates, sales cycles, forecast accuracy and AE/FDE pod productivity. A healthy pipeline consists of real buyers, clearly defined use cases, executable deployment paths and credible deal economics. Expansion should follow initial production success, not just an impressive proof of concept.

Early success means building an exceptional initial team, identifying a defensible set of priority markets and named accounts, personally helping progress lighthouse deals and establishing replicable wins. Longer term, we want a European enterprise organization that can forecast reliably and grow without requiring bespoke execution on every account.

#### Who you are

* You've built and led enterprise sales teams across multiple European markets and personally helped close substantial, complex B2B technology deals with large regional or multinational customers.
* You understand how European enterprises buy, including regional differences in procurement, security, data handling and decision-making. You can distinguish a real requirement from a sales objection and won't make unsupported compliance claims.
* You have technical fluency in areas such as cloud infrastructure, AI, networking, developer platforms or communications. You can work directly with FDEs and customer architects to turn a demanding evaluation into a production deployment.
* You know how to allocate coverage across countries and industries, recruit strong local talent and run a distributed organization with a consistent performance standard.
* You bring rigorous forecasting, genuine pipeline discipline, strong executive presence and a record of turning initial deployments into larger, multi-year relationships.
* You're a builder who still enjoys customers, recruiting and deals. You don't need a fully formed regional machine before you can produce results.

#### Why Telnyx

You will build a direct enterprise business across one of the world's most demanding markets, with meaningful ownership of regional strategy, team design and major customer relationships. The underlying technology is real, the company has scale and momentum, and you will work closely with senior technical and go-to-market leadership.

**Job Title:** Senior Consultant – NIS2 Cyber Governance, Risk & Compliance

**Location:** Dublin 2, Ireland; client office is the contractual home base.

**Start Date:** Anticipated November 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter, subject to award and confirmation.

**Contract Duration:** Anticipated 12 months plus up to two optional six-month extensions; duration units await client confirmation.

**Hybrid / Onsite / Remote:** Required on-site attendance and any hybrid or remote arrangement are to be confirmed.

**Grade and Experience:** Level 3 Senior Consultant; typically more than three years as a professional consultant, with specialist expertise and project/team management experience.

Grade experience is indicative, rather than a separate minimum-years pass/fail threshold.

# Client Overview

An Irish central government organisation is operationalising NIS2-aligned cybersecurity governance, risk and compliance following a gap analysis. Its existing eramba GRC platform requires configuration, integration and embedding; platform selection is outside scope.

# Role Overview

Lead governance, cyber risk, incident response, compliance, assurance and audit readiness. Combine strategic advice with hands-on delivery, oversee the Consultant’s platform work and lead stakeholder engagement and knowledge transfer.

# Mandatory Requirements and Experience

Candidates must meet the following role-specific sourcing requirements. These support the team’s overall capability and are not a statement that every item is an individual tender pass/fail test.

·         Proven NIS2 implementation or equivalent ISO/IEC 27001 / NIST CSF delivery.

·         Strong cyber GRC capability: governance, risk, control design/testing, assurance and audit readiness.

·         Comparable public-sector or regulated-environment engagements.

·         Strategic advice and hands-on implementation; GRC platform delivery oversight; client-facing project and stakeholder leadership.

  

 

# Availability

Confirm earliest start, available days, planned absences and ability to attend Dublin as agreed. Named personnel must remain available for the agreed term. Actual workload is unconfirmed; engagement is subject to contract award and client approval.

# Qualifications

No specific degree or certification is mandatory. Relevant qualifications and training are desirable. CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CGEIT, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer/Auditor or relevant NIS2 training; IMCA Member-level or similar accreditation is desirable.

# English Language Proficiency

Fluent spoken and written English for workshops, stakeholder communication, reporting, documentation and training. This is a recruitment expectation; no specific language test or score is prescribed.

# Key Deliverables

·         Operational governance structures, roles, reporting lines, decision forums and escalation paths.

·         Cyber risk processes embedded within enterprise risk management, including risk methodology, ownership and treatment oversight.

·         Incident response procedures, playbooks and tested capabilities aligned with reporting obligations.

·         NIS2 control framework, control ownership, testing methods, evidence standards and requirements-to-evidence traceability.

·         Assurance dashboards and reporting, audit-readiness documentation and quality assurance of platform outputs.

·         Delivery plan, milestones, risks/issues, dependencies, change control and stakeholder reporting.

·         Training materials, structured knowledge transfer and operational handover enabling independent client operation.

# Key Experience Competencies and Skillsets

Risk and control assessment; consulting and analytical methods; workshop facilitation; clear executive reporting; stakeholder and delivery leadership. GRC platform implementation knowledge is essential; hands-on eramba experience is desirable.

# Engagement and Working Arrangements

Working days and full-time/part-time commitment are to be confirmed. The 100 notional days per grade are for evaluation only and do not establish actual days or a two-day-per-week schedule. Extension workloads are also unconfirmed. One working day is 7.5 hours; part days are pro rata. Travel beyond the home base requires prior approval. Candidate daily rates are agreed separately.

**ABOUT AIREDALE**

 Airedale Group are the leading market design, installation, and maintenance provider for commercial kitchens in the UK hospitality and food service industry. We work alongside clients from the initial designs through to bespoke fabrication and installation. Coupled with the largest body of professional maintenance engineers in the country, we offer the complete end-to-end solution to our extensive client base. We have long-standing relationships with many of the biggest multi-site brands in the UK.

**ABOUT LIGHTHOUSE**

Lighthouse is Airedale Group's IoT platform for commercial kitchens. We monitor and control the equipment inside them — fryers, grills, ovens, refrigeration, boilers — across the estates of some of the UK's best-known restaurant and pub brands. Unusually, we do not only observe that equipment; we control it, which is why major customers trust us with live cooking assets.

Energy savings opened the door, but they are not the product. The same data already evidences food safety compliance, stock loss prevention, cleaning compliance, remote fault diagnosis and — most significantly — early warning of equipment failure. Our predictive proof of concept identified drift several days before failures were logged, validated against real engineer job history rather than synthetic data.

Our board has funded a dedicated data and analytics capability to turn that evidence into product. This role builds it.

**ABOUT THE ROLE**

As Senior IoT Data & AI Engineer, you will convert proven analysis into running systems. Working alongside our IoT data analyst, who holds the domain knowledge and customer relationships, you will build the data platform, the predictive models and the automated reporting that allow insight to be produced repeatedly rather than by hand.

The first priority is early failure detection. We have committed to delivering it for a major customer, and getting it into service — then proving how accurate it is — is your first quarter.

This is a hands-on role in a deliberately small team. You will work directly with the CTO and with our IoT data analyst, who is your closest working partner: they define what good looks like and validate that what you build is right; you make it repeatable. You will also collaborate with the wider Airedale group data team on shared standards as that function develops.

You will not be required to run the monthly customer reporting meetings — the analyst leads those — but you should expect to join customers periodically and for technical discussions. Engineers who never meet the customer build the wrong thing.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Take our anomaly detection work from proof of concept into production across the estate, moving from retrospective analysis to live early warning.
* Build the validation loop that joins every alert to the engineer's finding, so detection accuracy is measured rather than asserted.
* Develop the failure-signature library from telemetry crossed with twenty years of service history — the asset that makes our predictions defensible and that no competitor can replicate.
* Tune alerting continuously so it stays actionable and does not become noise.
* Own the flow from ThingsBoard, currently on managed hosting, into Microsoft Fabric — streaming ingest, full-history archive, and the conformed layer beneath everything else.
* Build the derived data layer: asset state classification, expected consumption and baselines, deviation scoring, an event register and governed metric definitions.
* Evaluate ThingsBoard Trends Analytics against building our own and make the recommendation on evidence — then implement it.
* Apply proper engineering discipline: version control, testing, reproducibility. Nothing should depend on a script on someone's laptop.
* Build with large language models as a core part of the role, not an experiment: generated report narratives, plain-language explanation of anomalies, and a conversational interface over our data.
* Deliver that interface against the governed data layer, with customer isolation enforced properly and an evaluation suite that proves answers are correct.
* Maintain the boundary that matters: figures are computed in the data layer and narrated by the model, never generated by it.
* Industrialise the customer reporting our analyst currently produces by hand, so that it scales as the estate grows rather than consuming more people.
* Publish analytics outputs to our customer portal through served APIs.

**EXPERIENCE REQUIRED**

* Strong Python and SQL, with production experience building and operating data pipelines — ideally in Microsoft Fabric, or a comparable lakehouse platform such as Databricks, Synapse or a dbt-based stack.
* Hands-on experience with time-series, sensor or telemetry data at scale, including the realities of gaps, drift, flatlines and misbehaving devices.
* Applied anomaly detection or predictive modelling taken into production, with the judgement to keep methods robust and explainable rather than elaborate.
* Practical experience building with LLM APIs beyond chat use: retrieval, tool use, generated reporting, and evaluation of model outputs.
* Self-directed and adaptable, comfortable owning delivery end to end in a small team without an engineering department to fall back on.
* Able to explain technical work clearly to non-technical colleagues and customers.

The Airedale Group is expanding rapidly, employing circa 700 people across multiple locations in the UK. This is a fantastic time to be joining the business with opportunities for career progression.

# Senior Backend Developer

Join our team at the Guardian and be a part of a diverse and inclusive global organisation that delivers fearless, investigative journalism and holds power to account. Our team of award-winning journalists, cutting-edge commercial professionals and industry-leading digital experts are committed to making a difference and represent a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. We offer a challenging and exciting environment for career development, with a focus on training, growth and fostering an inclusive culture.

We are now looking for a **Senior Backend Software Developer** to join our **Apps Experience** team on a 12 month fixed contract.

You could be building the products that showcase our progressive and independent journalism, crafting the tools that journalists use to write their stories, developing the services that allow those stories to be distributed across the globe, or safeguarding our financial future.

**About the role**

* You'll mostly be programming in Scala and Typescript, running in AWS, but we use the tool that best fits the problem.
* You'll be working in a cross-functional team, which is empowered to rapidly iterate and release new features.
* You won't be coding in isolation - our culture is strongly collaborative, whether pair programming with other developers or working closely with editorial and commercial colleagues.
* Sometimes deciding what code to write is as hard as writing the code itself. As an engineer you'll be involved in product decisions as well as technical ones.
* You have a strong interest in growing your skills even further.

Much of our code is openly available on GitHub, and some of our projects are widely used throughout the Open Source community. Many of our developers regularly attend and present at conferences. Please visit our Guardian Developers site and the Guardian Developer blog for more information about working in the Digital Development team.

**About you**

* As a full stack engineer, you'll be equally willing to dive into a purely functional and composable Scala back-end, or a complex Typescript front-end.
* You inspire the people you work with, and are inspired by them in return.
* You contribute to the direction of your team's products
* You are passionate about spreading engineering best practice beyond your immediate team.
* You are excited by the opportunity to shape the future of digital journalism.
* Your interests go beyond just your team's objectives; you are curious about where the organisation is moving as a whole.
* You have a strong interest in growing your skills.
* You can make reasoned choices regarding what technologies to use and when to use them.
* We believe diversity of people, backgrounds, experience and ideas helps us to build better products and achieve more. We welcome applicants who have taken traditional and non-traditional career paths into software development.

**We actively encourage applications from groups traditionally underrepresented in the UK media**

Our engineers and developers operate in a hybrid environment working 1 day a week from our offices in Kings Cross and 4 days a week remotely.

We strive for transparency in remuneration. The salary for new Senior Developers at the Guardian is £72,000 per year.

We value and respect all differences (seen and unseen) in all people. We aspire to have inclusive working experiences and an environment that reflects the audience we serve, where our people have equal access to career development opportunities, their voices are heard and can contribute to our future. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. Many of our staff work flexibly and we will consider all requests for flexible working arrangements.

**How to apply**

Please upload your CV and covering letter as one document. You should also highlight the extent to which your skills/experience meets the requirements of the role and your motivation behind applying.

Our interview process involves two stages: a face to face interview and a pairing test. We may offer a remote pairing test for candidates who would have to travel a long distance to our office in London, however you will have to arrange to come to our office for the face to face interview.

The closing date for applications is **Friday 30th October 2026.**

All roles at the Guardian are open for everybody to apply. It is important to us that you feel supported and comfortable throughout your recruitment process, in order to perform your best. Please let us know if there are any changes we could make to help your application, this includes providing documents in accessible formats or personalising the process to better support your needs. Please contact Anna Vipers on anna.vipers@guardian.co.uk to discuss further so we can work with you to support you through your application.

**Benefits at the Guardian**

You'll have 30 days of annual leave per year (plus bank holidays) with the option to purchase an additional 5 days. Our pension scheme is generous; if you contribute 5% then we will contribute 8-12% (depending on your age). We believe in giving back, which is why employees are given 2 volunteering days annually and the option of payroll giving. Season ticket loans are also available.

You are entitled to private healthcare, life cover, income protection, and eye tests. You can also opt in to dental insurance.

We have enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental leave policies in place. We also support our employees by offering an IVF, menopause, baby loss, and trans equality policy.

**Culture and wellbeing**

We want everyone to feel like they belong at the Guardian and we champion diversity of thought. Our various employee forums provide a platform to use their voice to foster an inclusive workplace. We became the first major media organisation to achieve B Corp status.

We offer tools to help you prioritise your wellbeing including access to our employee benefits platform which provides tailored support for health and wellbeing. In addition, we also offer free yoga and pilates classes. These run alongside our corporate gym membership and cycle to work scheme.

Our canteen has views overlooking the Regents Canal and caters for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

**Learning and development**

We encourage personal and professional growth. Employees have access to a broad range of tools and solutions, and we are happy to support the pursuit of professional qualifications through vocational courses and apprenticeships.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. You will expand TRM’s strategic access across the EMEA financial institution ecosystem.

This is a senior individual contributor role, designed for someone who already has deep credibility and trusted relationships across banks, and financial institutions. You are not being hired to build a network from scratch. You are being hired to activate a network you have already earned.

This is not a traditional closing-quota sales role. ## **Application Instructions**

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

## **Interviewing with TRM**

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

* **Recruiter Intro:** Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.
* **Hiring Manager:** Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

* Accelerate repeatable workflows
* Structure and solve problems
* Improve output quality
* Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

## **Life at TRM**

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

* Priorities and targets to change quickly
* Operating with a high degree of ambiguity
* A high level of personal ownership and accountability
* Close collaboration across teams and functions
* Frequent, high-touch communication
* Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking
* A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

## **Leadership Principles**

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

* Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.
* Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‐to‐end, and invest in getting better everyday.
* Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‐team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

## About the role

TRM is building a highly impactful, collaborative Environmental Crimes intelligence function, with one goal: disrupt the illicit actors behind wildlife trafficking and other environmental crimes, and add real friction to their ability to operate.

As our **Senior or Staff Intelligence Analyst, Environmental Crimes**, you will own TRM's intelligence on this category end-to-end. You will research, analyze, and publish intelligence on environmental crime networks and the crypto and financial flows behind them, combining on-chain tracing, OSINT, and off-chain data from partners into a picture that law enforcement, NGOs, and private-sector partners can act on.

You will also be the clear TRM owner for our partnership with United for Wildlife and Project Pangolin, serving a global network of partner organizations as a trusted advisor, convener, and the expert user who shapes how TRM's products serve this mission. What makes this role unique: you get to build a new intelligence category from the ground up, on the leading blockchain intelligence platform, with executive sponsorship and direct real-world impact.

## The impact you will have

* **Build the environmental crimes threat picture.** Research, author, and publish intelligence products (threat assessments, typology reports, trend analysis, actor profiles, network maps) on environmental crime and the illicit finance behind it, and maintain a reusable threat picture inside TRM's intelligence infrastructure.
* **Drive investigations to action.** Develop and use a wide variety of intelligence sources, tools, and capabilities — on-chain, OSINT, and partner-provided off-chain data — to identify the wallets, entities, and off-ramps behind environmental crime networks. Produce structured, source-cited targeting packages that support law enforcement and partner investigations and surface disruption opportunities.
* **Own the United for Wildlife partner program.** Replace fractional coverage with a managed, repeatable program across a network of 200+ partner organizations: case assistance, analysis, guidance, training, and onboarding.

* Production AI fluency: you already use AI and LLMs to accelerate research and analysis, build reusable workflows, and critically evaluate AI output — neither accept-all nor reject-all.

* Strong stakeholder communication, briefing, and facilitation skills.
* Self-directed: you thrive in ambiguity and generate visible wins quickly in an early-stage initiative.
* Commitment to becoming fluent in blockchain tracing and TRM's tooling. Prior crypto experience is not required; we will train you.

* Distributed, not distant: a global team that collaborates across time zones with regular overlap for syncs.
* Slack-first, async communication; @mention for timely responses.
* Weekly 1:1s and team syncs, plus case and partner-delivery rhythms.

# Full Stack Agentic Developer

## About Eidra UK

Eidra is a collective of around 1,600 people across design, technology, data and business transformation companies, including Umain, Kurppa Hosk, Above and Curamando. Eidra UK brings that capability together for UK clients from our London base.

Umain is the engineering practice inside Eidra UK. We design, build and run digital products at scale: apps with 400M+ downloads, platforms serving 50M+ monthly active users, and backends handling tens of thousands of requests per second.

We are building Eidra UK around an AI-first way of delivering software. This role sits at the centre of that.

## The role

We’re looking for a full stack developer who already works agentically. You write clear specs, run multiple agents in parallel against them, choose the right model for each job, and take full ownership of what ships.

You’ll work on client products end to end, from shaping requirements with stakeholders through to production. You’ll also help define how Eidra UK builds software with agents: the practices, tooling and standards the rest of the team uses.

## How we build

We start from a clear spec, break the work into tasks agents can complete, run those agents in parallel, verify the output with tests, evals and review, then ship. The spec is the source of truth. Agents do much of the implementation. You own the spec, the orchestration and the quality of the result.

## What you’ll do

**Spec driven delivery**

* Define requirements in a structured way: identify the actors, describe their use cases, then derive the features that serve them.
* Turn client needs into specs that both people and agents can build against: clear scope, acceptance criteria, interfaces and constraints.
* Keep specs, tests and code in step as the product changes.
* Break work into units that agents can complete and verify independently.

**Agent orchestration**

* Run and coordinate agent swarms: parallel agents, subagents and specialised roles (planning, implementation, review, testing).
* Build and maintain the supporting tooling: MCP servers, agent skills, prompts, context files and isolated workspaces.
* Design the checks that keep agent output trustworthy: test coverage, evals, guardrails and human review points.

**Model selection and mixing**

* Combine frontier and open-weight models to deliver results.
* Route work by capability, cost, latency and data sensitivity, including self-hosted or private deployments where client data requires it.
* Measure model performance on real tasks and change the mix when the evidence says so.

**Full stack engineering**

* Build secure, scalable web applications with TypeScript, React and Next.js.
* Build backend services and APIs with Node.js and NestJS.
* Create reusable UI components using design system principles.
* Work with cloud infrastructure (GCP, AWS or Azure), infrastructure as code with Terraform, and CI/CD pipelines.
* Build observable systems with metrics, logging and tracing, including for LLM and agent behaviour in production.

**Clients and team**

* Work directly with clients and cross-functional teams across design, product and data.
* Explain agentic delivery, its trade-offs and its limits to technical and non-technical audiences.
* Share what works: pair with colleagues, document patterns and help raise the agentic practice across Eidra UK.

## What we’re looking for

* 3+ years of professional full stack experience, with strong TypeScript, React/Next.js, Node.js and core web fundamentals.
* Hands-on experience delivering production software with coding agents (for example Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or similar), beyond autocomplete.
* Strong requirement definition experience, working from actors to use cases to feature definitions with clear acceptance criteria.
* A working spec driven development practice. You can show specs you’ve written and what agents built from them.
* Experience running multiple agents in parallel and coordinating their output.
* Practical experience using both frontier and open-weight models, with a view on when each is the right choice.
* Strong engineering judgement. You read and review agent output critically and you own the result as your own code.
* Comfort with ambiguity, and the consulting instinct to work it through with clients.
* Curiosity. The tools change monthly and you enjoy keeping up.

## Nice to have

* Building agentic features into client products: tool calling, RAG, MCP servers, multi-agent workflows.
* Running open-weight models in production (for example vLLM, Ollama or managed inference).
* LLM evaluation and observability tooling.
* Contributions to open source agent tooling or published writing on agentic engineering.
* Tailwind CSS, Storybook and design system work.
* Experience in a consultancy or agency setting.

## Working setup

London is the default office. You’ll work remotely when it suits the team or the client.

Don’t match every point? Apply anyway. We care more about how you think and what you’ve built than about ticking every box.

## Unilever Future Leadership Programme - Data & Analytics UK

Our Future Leaders Programme will ignite the leader in you. This unique programme is designed to develop Unilever’s Future Leaders (UFLs) by providing challenging and purposeful opportunities that accelerate their readiness to take on business leadership roles.

The Unilever Future Leaders Program (UFLP) is a global initiative enabling Unilever to build a strong talent pipeline that will support and lead our business growth.  In the UK, our UFLP is a 36-month rotational leadership development program for which we recruit top-performing undergraduate talent who demonstrate the potential to become managers within our business.  It’s designed to grow you into a manager, through hands-on learning alongside world-class experts. You’ll be hired into a function and develop your leadership skills by working on live projects which offer you all the experience you need to become ready for your first management role.  At the heart of it, it’s about developing tomorrow’s leaders, today. 

From Day 1, you will take on real business challenges within your own function and across the organization. Along the way you will develop deep core professional skills and leadership skills, and build a robust support network.  On top of all that, you will have a lot of fun along the journey.

We look for people who want to get to grips with the inner workings of a vast business and a desire to understand how it works. It’s about commitment, real people skills and a deep-seated interest in the business as a whole. You’ll become part of a leading-edge company, where you’ll work with outstanding brands and outstanding people to drive sustainable business growth.

**Your Future Employer**

  

Unilever is one of the world's leading FMCG companies, home to iconic brands including Dove, Vaseline, TRESemmé, Lynx, Persil, Domestos, Surf, Radox, Sure and Liquid I.V. Through products used by millions of people every day, we help improve health, wellbeing, confidence and care around the world.

  

Established over 100 years ago, Unilever has a proud heritage of innovation and a long-standing belief that great brands, great people and responsible business go hand in hand.

  

Today, we are transforming into a faster, more focused growth company centred on Beauty & Wellbeing, Personal Care and Home Care. Through world-class brands, cutting-edge science and technology, digital innovation and AI-enabled capabilities, we are building unmissably superior products and experiences for consumers around the world.

  

A career at Unilever offers the opportunity to work at global scale while helping shape the future of some of the world's most recognised brands. Our people are at the heart of everything we do, bringing curiosity, creativity and passion to solve real business challenges and make a meaningful impact every day.

  

***\*As we receive a high volume of applications, please make sure to read the job descriptions on our website carefully and apply for the ONE function you are most interested in. Only your first application will be considered\**** 

  

**What we’re looking for?**

  

We’re looking for curious, purpose‐driven graduates who are excited by how AI is evolving our data, brands and operations and who want to keep learning every day. You don’t need to be an expert yet and we welcome applicants from all degree backgrounds. However, you do need a real interest in data and analytics, a growth mindset, and the confidence to ask good questions. If you enjoy challenging the status quo, spotting patterns in data, communicating clearly, and are comfortable with ambiguity, you’ll thrive here Integrity matters to us: you’ll show good judgement, take ownership, and be comfortable balancing pace with care when the stakes are high.

  

**What will the programme involve?**

  

You’ll complete six rotations, each lasting six months, allowing you to gain both depth and breadth of experience.

  

**You will:**

* Participate in a leadership development programme designed to accelerate your growth and prepare you to become one of Unilever’s future leaders.

* Specialise in Technology or Cyber Security or Data & Analytics.

* Complete rotations within your chosen area to build core expertise.

* May have the opportunity to work outside your chosen track (e.g. marketing, supply chain, customer development).
* Be flexible on the scheme and work across offices in Kingston upon Thames, London and Port Sunlight (near Liverpool) depending on the rotation.

* Be supported with a dedicated mentor, who is an expert in your chosen stream and will guide you throughout the programme.

* Shape the scheme through our graduate-led pillars, such as wellbeing, learning and development and placement success. These pillars are run by current graduates and play a key role in shaping the UFLP experience.

  

Please see further information on the **Data & Analytics** stream below:

  

In this specialized stream, you will delve into the fascinating world of Data & Analytics, collaborating on real business projects and building expertise in cutting-edge cloud and rapidly advancing AI technologies. As AI continues to evolve at extraordinary speed, ensuring our data is high quality, trusted, and ready is more important than ever. Unleashing the power of data, you'll play a pivotal role in strategic delivery, unlocking invaluable insights for our business.

  

At Unilever, our commitment to data democratization empowers business users across the globe to make confident, data-driven choices. This pervasive shift facilitates informed decision-making across all aspects of our business, identifying granular growth opportunities and propelling us to outperform the market. Your journey within the program will encompass diverse experiences in data analytics, data science, data engineering, and business partnering, as you leverage and maximize the vast scale of information available at Unilever.

  

**What could your day-to-day role include (depending on your role)?**

  

Day to day, you could be helping prepare our data lakehouses for AI by improving data quality, structure and accessibility, ensuring the information within them is ready to fuel advanced analytics and machine learning. You could partner with teams across the business to create meaningful dashboards, strengthen data pipelines, and analyse rich datasets to reveal insights that guide important decisions. You could be working with some of our strategic technology partners like Google and Microsoft to deliver large scale global programmes, or with niche technology start-ups and industry innovators to solve current business and sustainability challenges. Your work will directly contribute to making Unilever’s data landscape more intelligent, scalable and AI ready.

  

**Some of the teams you could be allocated to include**:

  

* Data Science

* Artificial Intelligence Centre of Excellence Team

* Data Strategy Team

* Cross-operations

* Data & AI Change Management

  

**Skills required include:**

  

* Curiosity about AI

* Foundational cloud computing awareness

* Interest in statistics

* Basic programming knowledge

  

Please note, that at Unilever, we have development programmes, the skills below are skills that would be good to have at the beginning however you will develop them throughout the programme.

  

* Stakeholder Analysis / Management / Business Partnering

* Product Management

* Systems Thinking

* Artificial Intelligence

* Risk Management

* Project Management / Agile Delivery

* Change Management & Activation

* Strategic Thinking

* Third Party Management

  

**Our application process involves:**

  

Step 1: Online Application

  

Complete the online application form. It is a simple and easy application process with the option of filling out your details using your LinkedIn profile. You may apply to one function in your application.

  

Step 2: Profile Assessment 

  

Complete two stages of profile assessment; a portrait personality test and an online assessment. These are designed to look at different elements of your cognitive, emotional, and social traits. You will receive personalised feedback after completing each stage.

  

Step 3: Digital Interview

  

The digital interview will consist of 3 short questions followed by a business case. You will be asked to solve real-world problems using Unilever scenarios. You’ll be able to record and complete your interview anytime and anywhere.

*\*Please note, we do not use AI as a screening tool in our recruitment process therefore, your digital interview submission will be reviewed by a real person\**

  

Step 4: Discovery Center

  

Ahead of the Discovery Centre, you will be invited to complete a short online assessment via Alooba, designed to give you the opportunity to demonstrate your technical capabilities.

  

You will then be invited to a ‘day in the life’ of a Future Leader at Unilever. You will get to experience a face-to-face day filled with several exciting activities including project meetings, business challenges, a team meeting with Unilever colleagues, and an interview.

  

**What Can Unilever offer YOU?**

  

* A Competitive Salary of £35,000

* A Benefits Envelope which has a notional value of 25% of your pensionable earnings. Use it to save for your pension, get extra taxable pay or both.

* A pension Scheme

* Annual Bonus

* A discounted staff shop

* Subsidised Gym Memberships - availability varies by site

* Shares

* Relocation support through a £5000 tax free loan

* 25 days of holiday allowance

  

To find out more about Future Careers at Unilever UK, check out our Instagram page!

  

Diversity at Unilever is about championing inclusion, embracing differences, creating possibilities, and growing together for better business performance.

The Junior Analyst will support the S&P / Strategy team in tracking the secondhand, newbuilding and demolition markets, analysing potential acquisitions and identifying areas for investment across tanker and dry bulk. ·         Assess valuations against recent comparables and model earnings potential to test the investment case for each candidate.

·         Prepare clear, well-supported acquisition recommendations for review by the Head of Strategy and senior team members.

**Investment Research**

·         Research segments, vessel types and market trends to identify areas for investment and support the company's investment strategy.

·         Maintain and develop the vessel sales register, asset value database, and fleet and market databases, taking ownership of data quality.

The Service Holder will be responsible for the design activities under his/her scope and approval of the material selection, corrosion, welding & NDE/NDT activities and technical matters related to the SURF package of the Venus project.

This will include but not be limited to reviewing, approving, preparing and managing all studies, drawings specifications, procedures, ... from the SURF Contractor, Suppliers and Sub-Suppliers documentation related to the Service Holder field of expertise during EPCI phases.

The Service Holder shall also assist the umbilical and flexible Specialists in all matters related to the Service Holder field of expertise.

The projects consist of Steel Lazy Wave Risers (SLWR), rigid flowlines and rigid spools in CS and CRA lined pipe (WOL/MLP/HRB) and rigid jumpers in Duplex, and associated subsea structures, equipment and ancillaries, for a very deep-water oil greenfield project.

The Service Holder will also provide support to the SURF Technical Manager and the SURF team and liaise with other project package teams (SPS and FPSO).

· Promote & comply with all activities with applicable safety instructions and other company H3SE&Q rules, implement and control H3SE rules and requirements within his area of responsibility. • Positive, constructive, proactive and pragmatic mindset.

• Ability to work within large teams with other parties (Contractors, suppliers, HQ technical teams, etc.).

• Previous experience within a complex and multicultural working environment.
